title: BREAKING: Eetha passed by CBFC with U/A 16+ certificate; beats Saaho by JUST 22 seconds to become the LONGEST film of Shraddha Kapoor’s 16-year career
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As per the website of the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC), Eetha was passed on November 27 with a U/A 16+ certificate. The length of the movie, as mentioned on the website, is 172 minutes and 14 seconds. In other words, Eetha is 2 hours, 52 minutes and 14 seconds long.

Adding to this, This makes Eetha the longest movie of Shraddha Kapoor's illustrious 16-year career. Interestingly, it is longer than Saaho (2019) by just 22 seconds! The Prabhas co-starrer, which was rolled out as a Pan-India movie, had a runtime of 171 minutes and 52 seconds, that is, 2 hours, 51 minutes and 52 seconds.

Meanwhile, Besides Shraddha Kapoor, Eetha also stars Randeep Hooda, Mohd. Zeeshan Ayyub, Siddharth Jadhav, Ishtiyak Khan and Anant Joshi. A Maddock Films and Kathputli Creations production, Eetha is produced by Dinesh Vijan, Laxman Utekar and Karishma Sharma. It marks Laxman Utekar's next directorial venture after the smash hit Chhaava (2025).

Notably, Eetha features Shraddha Kapoor in the role of legendary Marathi Tamasha artiste Vithabai Narayangaonkar. The movie was originally scheduled to rollout in cinemas on August 28 on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan and will now arrive in theatres on December 4.

As per the latest buzz, Interestingly, even before its theatrical rollout, Eetha has already made its way into the record books. Earlier this week, the movie entered both the India Book of Records and the Asia Book of Records. The recognition came after 517 women performed the Lavani hook steps from the movie's first song, ‘ Ji Ji Re Ji ’, in perfect synchrony for one minute.

In further updates, 5 longest films of Shraddha Kapoor: 1. Eetha - 2 hours and 52 minutes 2. Saaho - 2 hours and 51 minutes 3. Batti Gul Meter Chalu - 2 hours and 43 minutes 4. Haider - 2 hours and 42 minutes 5. Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar - 2 hours and 39 minutes

title: BREAKING: You CANNOT see everything in You Can See Everything; CBFC CENSORS 12 seconds nudity visual DESPITE ‘A’ certificate
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As per the censor certificate uploaded by Mumbai Subtitles Database (a popular social media handle that informs movie buffs about which cinemas are playing South and international films with subtitles in the city), a 12-second visual of nudity, which appears at the 22 nd minute, has been completely axed by the Examining Committee of the CBFC. This is despite the movie receiving an adults-only certificate. The other change asked by the CBFC was to insert an anti-smoking awareness video in the beginning and before the second half and to insert anti-smoking and anti-alcohol tickers in scenes of cigarette and liquor consumption.

Adding to this, Once the changes were made, the CBFC passed You Can See Everything on November 20. The length of the movie, as mentioned on the censor certificate, is 176.08 minutes. In other words, You Can See Everything is 2 hours, 56 minutes and 8 seconds long.

Meanwhile, You Can See Everything is about Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of the defunct health technology company Theranos, and her partner Billy Evans. They invite a movie crew to document them nearly a month before Elizabeth is sentenced to imprisonment for 11 years for defrauding investors. It has been rolled out in India by Sony Pictures Films India Pvt Ltd.

Notably, You Can See Everything was rolled out theatrically in most markets on October 16 and has grossed $107 million against a $7 million production budget. As per Wikipedia, it is the ninth highest-grossing documentary movie of all time.

As per the latest buzz, In India, You Can See Everything collected Rs. 19.42 lakhs on its opening day, outperforming the other new Hollywood releases of November 27. Hexed and Focker-In-Law collected Rs. 17.80 lakhs and Rs. 9.78 lakhs, respectively. Paper Tiger fared even lower, earning just Rs. 4.38 lakhs, while Victorian Psycho managed to collect Rs. 3 lakhs.

title: EXCLUSIVE: No cuts, no modifications, not even additional disclaimers! Salman Khan’s Maatrubhumi gets U/A 16+ certificate; CBFC chairman personally signs the certificate
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

However, an industry insider explained, “The movie went through certain changes as asked by the Government of India. The makers made those changes and showed it to the relevant authorities. They okayed it, after which the movie was submitted to the CBFC, as is the process. Since the government authorities had already given their nod, the CBFC found no reason to make any further changes or modifications.”

Adding to this, Another interesting aspect of Maatrubhumi ’s censor certification is the signature on the certificate. Usually, the CEO of the CBFC, Rajendra Singh Shekhawat, digitally signs the censor certificate. However, in the case of Maatrubhumi , the certificate has been signed by none other than the CBFC chairman, Shashi Shekhar Vempati. This could possibly be among the first instances of a censor certificate bearing the signature of the new CBFC chairman.

Meanwhile, Maatrubhumi was passed by the CBFC on November 18 with a U/A 16+ rating. The length of the movie, as mentioned on the censor certificate, is 154.12 minutes. In other words, Maatrubhumi is 2 hours, 34 minutes and 12 seconds long.

title: Shah Rukh Khan recalls calling co-star “beti” amid the shoot of romantic scene: “I started feeling I should play my age, which is 61 now”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

During his conversation with filmmaker Karan Johar at the event, SRK recalled that becoming a leading man had been a personal ambition since he entered the movie industry. He shared, "I did King because I always felt that I always wanted to be a hero. I'll tell you the reason, because when I joined the movie industry, I felt that I was not good-looking. I thought that when I get a chance to be a hero, I just took it very personally. That someone who is so simple-looking as I am, can become a hero. So I hold it very dearly that I always have to play the hero."

Adding to this, The star also spoke about an incident from a movie shoot that made him reconsider the age difference between himself and the actresses he was paired with. Recalling a romantic scene without identifying the movie or the people involved, he shared how the moment took an unexpected turn when he asked the star, "And one more thing, did you finish your tomorrow morning's math homework, daughter?"

Meanwhile, The incident made Khan reflect on the kind of roles he wanted to take up going forward. He shared, "The age difference became so much between the girls I was acting with, that I started feeling I should play my age, which is 61, and be as cool as a 61-year-old can be. So even today, if I sit down or stand up and say any of the dialogues, it still seems relevant. Because my daughter Suhana is also in the movie, all the girls in the world think, 'mera dad aisa bana tha'."
Notably, Explaining his curiosity behind King , he added, "So that's the reason for King . I just wanted to do it out of (curiosity). Am I still a hero at 60 and play my age?"
As per the latest buzz, Directed by Siddharth Anand, King is scheduled to rollout in cinemas worldwide on December 24, 2026.

title: Namit Malhotra denies that Ravana was glorified in Ramayana Part 1; says people liked demon king due to Yash
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Yash, who co-produced Ramayana with Namit Malhotra, also played Ravana in the movie. more Namit Malhotra says Ramayana doesn’t have praise for Ravana On DD News, Namit was asked to address criticism over supposedly glorifying Ravana in Ramayana. Denying the claims, the producer shared, “We have not shown that Ravana is good. What people have liked is Yash’s performance, who is a superstar. Ravana has not done any good deeds in the movie. He has wreaked havoc and terrorised so many people that Lord Ram had to intervene to stop him. People also need to understand that we have made a universal movie. Nowhere did we praise Ravana. We have only shown his journey from childhood as Dashanan and how someone like him became so powerful as Ravana.”

Adding to this, He also reiterated Ravana’s story to those confused, stating that despite receiving boons from the Gods, the king eventually met his downfall. “But there’s something more important that nobody has asked me till date. If Ravana is such a bad person, then why would Lord Brahma and Lord Shiva bless him? When God Himself has blessed him, he must have done something to deserve it. But that’s not the point. The point has always been that when God gives you everything and your ego takes you to the peak where you believe whatever you do is right, that’s the downfall. It’s Ravana’s ego that kills him,” shared Namit.

Meanwhile, While Ravana has often been depicted as a lustful, greedy king in Ramayana adaptations, Ramayana: Part 1 shows the backstory. It shows how a gifted musician is pushed by his mother at a young age to seek power for his people. Years of deep meditation and later, years of war, turn a young Dashanan into a powerful Ravana. Ravana is shown as someone who respects women when he chides his brother-in-law in a scene. He’s also shown to be the kind of king who wants his subjects to live like his equals. The events of the first movie end with Ravana seeking revenge by abducting Sita after his sister Surpanaka is disfigured by Lakshman. Ramayana: Part 2 will be rolled out in theatres for Diwali 2028.

title: Javed Akhtar says film music is reflective of society as he addresses criticism for Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi song Teri Sexy Beauty
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Javed Akhtar shared that songs like Teri Sexy Beauty don't exist in a void but are reflective of society. more Javed Akhtar points out movie music doesn’t exist in a void Javed was asked about the quality of Bollywood song lyrics on Music 91 by BCC’s YouTube channel and shared, “The movie industry and movie music don’t exist in a void. They are also part of society. Today, whether it's Gen Z or those older than them, their vocabulary isn’t as great as their parents' or grandparents’. Their vocabulary has shrunk. Language is, of course, for communication. But it’s a fine art in itself. It has beauty and elegance, depending on how you use it. Language is an art; it’s not just a vehicle for communication. But where is the attention to our language today? How many people read literature and poetry today?”

Adding to this, The lyricist also shared that greed for profit has changed things, adding that he still holds out hope though: “Society has become utility-oriented. And the definition of profit is whether it can be put in and drawn from the bank. If not, what’s the use for it? The depth of music, art and literature has been marginalised. But let me also give credit where it’s due. Today’s young people are getting back to it, no thanks to us. They are trying to discover all this on their own. So, I am not pessimistic at all. After ten to fifteen years, some major revival will happen.”

Meanwhile, Teri Sexy Beauty is composed and features lyrics by Sajid Khan. Salman sang the number with Muskaan. When the song was rolled out, many questioned why a war movie like Maatrubhumi required a romantic number. “I know everyone’s wondering how Teri Sexy Beauty fits into Maatrubhumi. Isn’t it on everyone’s mind? You will understand how it fits when you watch the movie. It comes on when an officer and several soldiers praise their wives. Whatever songs we’ve shown you, those visuals will be quite few in the movie,” explained Salman at the movie’s trailer launch.

title: How Vishal Chaturvedi's 28-day road trip helped 'Hanuman Ansh' become a phenomenon
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

How Vishal Chaturvedi's 28-day road trip helped 'Hanuman Ansh' become a phenomenon more The movie, a retelling of the life of Uttarakhand's revered saint Baba Neem Karoli, whose real name was Lakshman Narayan Sharma, has emerged as one of the year's biggest success stories, ranking among the most profitable films in cinema history.

Adding to this, "In terms of profit margins, 'Obsession' has profited 500 times of its investment. 'Hanuman Ansh' made 265 times our budget. I read in a couple of newspapers; they have done some research that the movie is the all-time most profitable Hindi movie," Chaturvedi, who made the movie on a modest budget of ₹ 1.7 crore rupees, told PTI in an interview.

Meanwhile, "Hanuman Ansh" was rolled out in theatres on August 7 without much fanfare and virtually no promotions. The movie struggled to draw audiences in its first two weeks, with collections ranging between ₹ 5 lakh and ₹ 20 lakh, according to trade website Sacnilk. And then it started picking up.

Notably, "'Spider-Man' was already there and was doing good. And there was one more movie with us, which got rolled out. It was 'Oh My Dog'. Then next week, 'Batwara 1947' and 'Awarapan 2' came in. So we were literally sandwiched between these big films. We were the smallest one.

As per the latest buzz, "We felt, 'Oh, this is going to go down the drain.' There were 25 theatres that were playing the movie and even they might remove it next week. So, we might not see 22nd of August," he added.
In further updates, Chaturvedi shared he and his team went on an Independence Day road trip on August 15 that took them across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Delhi-NCR and parts of Uttar Pradesh.
On top of that, Over the next 28 days, they visited theatres, temples and religious trusts, encouraging people to watch and spread the word about the movie.

"We travelled 28 days nonstop. We covered one city a day, where we went to a few theatres and maybe temples and big trusts like that. We started from Harni Hanuman Mandir in Vadodara and then Kashtabhanjan Hanuman Mandir in Ahmedabad. We kept going to these places.

title: Shah Rukh Khan says starring with much younger actresses made him want to embrace his age in King, now wants to be a cool 61-year-old hero
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shah Rukh Khan went grey-haired for his role in Siddharth Anand's King. more Shah Rukh Khan on acting with much younger actresses and being cool Shah Rukh spoke about why he wanted to star in King. “I’ve always wanted to be a hero. I felt I wasn’t good-looking when I first entered the movie industry. So, when I got the chance to be a hero, for someone as simple-looking as I am, I hold it very dearly,” he explained.

Adding to this, “Secondly, I was shooting for a movie which I won’t name, but Karan knows. I won’t name the director and heroine either. I was standing in front of her and telling her one of my amazing love dialogues,” he shared, adding, “I love you a lot; I want to get lost in your eyes. I feel like I’ve seen the world when I look at you. And one more thing: I hope you finished your math homework for tomorrow, beti (daughter). So, with the age difference between me, and the girls I was acting with, I started feeling I should play my age, which is 61 now. And be as cool as a 61-year-old can be.”

Meanwhile, Shah Rukh shared that, with his grey-haired look in King, he wanted girls to look at him differently now. “So, even if today I sit down or stand up and say any of the dialogue, it still seems relevant. And all the girls in the world, because my daughter Suhana is also part of the movie, all the girls think, this is how my dad should be. I just wanted to be a hero at 60 and play my age,” shared the star.

Notably, King is directed by Siddharth Anand , who co-wrote the screenplay with Sujoy Ghosh, Suresh Nair, and Sagar Pandya. It will mark Shah Rukh’s daughter, Suhana Khan’s, theatrical debut. Abhishek Bachchan, Deepika Padukone, Anil Kapoor, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahlawat, Jackie Shroff, Arshad Warsi, Raghav Juyal and Abhay Verma also star in it. Kareena Kapoor appears in the song Daddy Cool , which was rolled out on Friday. The movie will be rolled out in theatres on December 24.

The track was unveiled at Meta’s House of Instagram 2026, an event attended by more than 700 content creators from across the country. title: IFFI 2026: BookMyShow COO Ashish Saksena says theatrical cinema is ‘not fading away’, believes it will coexist with OTT
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Saksena shared his views during a panel discussion titled ‘ One Movie, Multiple Paydays: Extracting a Movie’s Full Value ’ , where he discussed the changing cinema landscape and the opportunities available to the industry. Reflecting on the theatrical business in 2026, he shared audiences continue to seek out films that offer a compelling experience on the big screen.

Adding to this, “Audiences today have more entertainment choices than ever before. Yet, the desire to experience a compelling story on the big screen, surrounded by an audience, remains deeply relevant. Theatres offer something that goes beyond watching a movie. They create a shared cultural experience that cannot quite be replicated elsewhere,” he shared.
Meanwhile, Saksena added, “The theatrical business in India is not fading away. If anything, it is finding newer reasons to thrive.”

Notably, He also spoke about BookMyShow's role in the cinema ecosystem, including how audience insights and market intelligence can help filmmakers and producers understand a movie's reach and reception. According to Saksena, the platform's involvement extends beyond ticketing and theatrical discovery.

As per the latest buzz, He pointed to BookMyShow Stream, the company's transactional video-on-demand (TVOD) service, as another avenue for films to reach audiences after their theatrical rollout. He also mentioned the Red Lorry Movie Festival (RLFF), which provides independent and distinctive cinema with curated screening opportunities.

In further updates, Looking ahead, Saksena shared technological developments and improvements in theatrical presentation could give audiences more reasons to visit cinemas. He cited premium formats, enhanced viewing technologies and immersive sound as areas that could contribute to the experience.

On top of that, Addressing the relationship between theatrical releases and streaming platforms, he shared both models can continue to operate alongside each other. “OTT and theatrical cinema can, and will, coexist. While one offers convenience and choice, the other will continue to draw audiences with its scale, spectacle and collective emotion,” he shared.

title: I&B Ministry seeks Netflix’s response over Sukesh Chandrashekhar documentary in seven days ahead of December 18 release
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

In a communication dated November 27, 2026, the Ministry forwarded the representation submitted by Advocate Anant Malik to Netflix Entertainment Services India and asked the streaming platform to examine the issues raised in it. The Ministry has sought Netflix's comments within seven days of receiving the communication.

Adding to this, The letter, bearing reference number J-11013/19/2025-DM, refers to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, and other applicable Indian laws. It also draws attention to the Code of Ethics governing digital news publishers and OTT platforms, which provides for a three-tier mechanism to address grievances concerning violations of the prescribed framework.

Meanwhile, The Ministry further noted that OTT platforms are required not to transmit content prohibited by law and to exercise due caution and discretion. The communication was signed by Kshitij Aggarwal, Deputy Director (Digital Media), and issued with the approval of the competent authority.

Notably, The representation was submitted by Malik on behalf of Chandrashekhar, who is currently in judicial custody at Mandoli Jail in Delhi. It raises objections to the documentary being rolled out before the conclusion of the criminal trials involving him.

As per the latest buzz, As reported earlier, Chandrashekhar's legal team had also issued a notice to Netflix and other parties associated with the documentary, seeking a postponement of its rollout until prosecution evidence in the pending cases is concluded. The notice raised concerns about the portrayal of allegations that are yet to be tested in court and the potential impact on the right to a fair trial.

In further updates, Importantly, the Ministry's latest communication does not direct Netflix to stop, postpone or withdraw the documentary. It has asked the platform to respond to the representation within the stipulated period. Netflix's response and the Ministry's subsequent course of action are awaited.

On top of that, The development comes amid growing scrutiny of how true-crime documentaries portray individuals facing ongoing criminal proceedings, particularly in relation to the presumption of innocence and the right to a fair trial.

On top of that, “Designing the scene in your head is important. We want to understand the star’s intellect. Please do your homework. If you understand life, you can understand acting,” shared Chhabra as quoted in a press note.

On self-tapes, his advice was to choose a clean background, ensure good lighting and clear sound, use someone who can deliver cues naturally, and frame the shot close enough to capture the face and eyes.

title: ‘Sita ma, how pretty she should look’: Sai Pallavi is unbothered by all the chatter about her Ramayana look, called herself most secure human being
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Ramayana features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama with Sai Pallavi as Sita. more In the first instalment of the two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic, Pallavi featured alongside Ranbir Kapoor, who featured as Lord Ram, Ravie Dubey in the role of Lakshman and Yash as Ravana, among others

Adding to this, "My life has always been about moving from one movie to another. It does bring some sort of a change to you because you carry a bit of the role in your heart. I've had a few changes (in me), but they all are very personal, and I don't think it is something that the world would understand or should even know. It is not even a bigger deal," the star shared when asked how her life has changed after playing Sita.
Meanwhile, Pallavi was in conversation with Barkha Dutt at the We the Women event in Mumbai.
Notably, The star, who primarily works in Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam films, also addressed online scrutiny surrounding her casting and appearance as Sita.

As per the latest buzz, "I'm not blind to social media things that are out there, like, 'Sita ma, how pretty she should look', and all of that, but if it shakes your core, then I think the flaw lies there, and you need to get stronger," she shared.

In further updates, "I think I'm as secure as any human being can be, and opinions are opinions. So, growing up if you've some sort of insecurity, you just need to make sure you are strong within, and you can fight the rest of the world or shut the noise out," she added.
On top of that, When asked about the characters she wouldn't want to essay, the 34-year-old star shared she refuses to play characters reduced to being just a glamorous face.

"If it is just going to be a part that is used as a tool for glamour or something that is replaceable, I wouldn't want to be that. I always look for strength in a character. So, over time, when you put your foot down and you do not want to do certain things, that itself speaks for itself, and after that you start getting roles that have some substance," she shared, adding that it was difficult to reject such roles in the beginning of her career.

title: Gunmaaster G9 review: Emraan Hashmi's guns cannot save this painfully familiar action thriller
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Gunmaaster G9 stars Emraan Hashmi in the lead role. This is the plot not just of Awarapan 2, Emraan Hashmi 's last cinematic outing just earlier this year, but also of his latest, Gunmaaster G9. Originality has clearly taken a long vacation for Christmas.

Adding to this, Directed by Aditya Datt, the movie revolves around Eshwar (Emraan), a dairy business owner who is approached by inspector Rana (Abhishek Singh) to help him bust a drug cartel led by Desu (Aparshakti Khurana). When Eshwar refuses, Rana threatens to reveal his dark past to his family, comprising his wife Aarti ( Genelia D'Souza ) and daughter Jiya (Inayat Verma). And so, there he goes again, picking up his guns and blasting heads off.

Meanwhile, Writers Sarim Momin and Junaid Wasi bring absolutely nothing new to the table. This is a story we can predict right down to the T. The movie begins on an overwhelmingly familiar note, helped only by an interesting antagonist played by Aparshakti. He is the only one who seems to treat this movie as an opportunity to showcase a different side of himself as an star. (Incidentally, both brothers, Ayushmann and Aparshakti, have had a movie rollout on the same Friday, the other being Yeh Prem Mol Liya .)

Notably, An Emraan Hashmi crime drama, until now, guaranteed at least one thing: good music. Gunmaaster G9, however, wastes its entire first half with practically no memorable music to speak of. So, essentially, there is very little left to excite the viewer. The second half offers more screen time to Genelia, whose character has a dark past of her own. This is when the movie finally gets interesting, leading to a crackling action sequence led by her. Alas, barring these moments, the narrative slips back into predictable territory, eventually setting things up for a sequel.
As per the latest buzz, Another area where the movie falters is its excessive flashbacks, which do little to enhance the storytelling and only interrupt its flow.

In further updates, The cinematography by Keiko Nakahara and Anik Ram Verma is good. I wish I could say the same about Himesh Reshammiya 's music, especially considering the beautiful melodies he has composed for the other rollout this Friday, Yeh Prem Mol Liya.

On top of that, In the performance department, this is quintessential Emraan Hashmi. But apart from the 'dard' that defined his character in Awarapan 2, you would struggle to tell one difference between Shivam in that movie and Eshwar in this one. Genelia makes the most of what she is given, while Aparshakti is quite effective as the unhinged villain. Abhishek Singh, meanwhile, is just about okay.

Overall, the biggest problem with Gunmaaster G9 is not that it follows a familiar template. Bollywood has never shied away from revisiting successful formulas. It is that the movie makes very little effort to disguise how familiar everything feels. From the brooding protagonist with a dark past to the protective father who will go to any lengths for his family, there is hardly a surprise here. Even Emraan's presence, which should ideally be the movie's biggest selling point, offers little novelty. The occasional action high and Genelia's interesting turn in the second half provide some relief, but not enough to rescue a movie that runs out of ammunition rather early. And with a sequel already being teased, one can only hope the writers find some fresh ideas before loading their guns again.

title: Shraddha Kapoor gained 10-12 kg for Eetha, pushed through gruelling rehearsals, recalls choreographer Vaibhavi Merchant
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shraddha Kapoor in a still from Eetha. Shraddha Kapoor gained 10-12 kilos for climax sequence Speaking about the preparations, Vaibhavi shared Shraddha had gained around 10 to 12 kilos for that stage of her character. She told Variety India, “Laxman Utekar (director) decided to shoot in reverse order, starting with the second half and the climax song first. That meant preparing Shraddha after she had gained roughly 10 to 12 kilos for that stage of the character. Extra weight increases strain on the knees, calves, and stamina during fast transitions, so we pushed through grueling rehearsals and conditioning, taking it hour by hour.”

Adding to this, Vaibhavi further opened up that Shraddha suffered a serious injury on the second day of shooting. The incident took place just before lunch, when the star was dancing barefoot on a floor that had become warm due to the daytime heat, leading to friction and the risk of injury.

Meanwhile, "It rattled everyone’s morale, but after a six-week to two-month break and strict physiotherapy, we returned with renewed focus and built mandatory warm-up, cool-down, and physio protocols around every subsequent Lavani," she added.

Notably, Earlier, at the launch of the song Ji Ji Re Ji in Pune, Laxman Utekar had lauded Shraddha’s dedication to the movie. He opened up that the star rehearsed with 8 kg ghungroos for 25 days for the movie. He shared, "Shraddha rehearsed for each song for 25 days with 4 kg ghungroo on each leg for eight hours. Her feet used to get swollen. She immersed herself in the world of Tamasha and Lavani to understand its depth and learn the art form. The first day of the song shoot went well. But on the second day, Shraddha had a muscle tear, and we had to halt the shoot."

title: Sai Pallavi didn't want to look airbrushed while playing real women on screen, says directors have no issue with her no-makeup look
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Sai Pallavi at the premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) more What Sai Pallavi shared The star shared, "This has been a conversation that everybody has brought up over the last 10 years. To be honest, I was insecure in the beginning of my career, but over time you realise that there is some sort of a movie between the actual audience and the people who are performing. Because I think the audience wants to consume something that is real and I have picked roles which have real women in real situations. So you would not want to look airbrushed, where people would not want to connect with the character. I have always been true to the characters and the directors have never seen anything wrong with that."

Adding to this, She added, “Over time I did learn to be myself. It is all your own. Right now, I have some lip gloss, an eye liner and some moisturizer on. This is not to flaunt, but if I have a layer of foundation or concealer I feel like a different person and it does not work for me. That is as simple as that, and if you feel good wearing makeup, then its your call. You should not have to fit yourself in a box to be a certain way.”

Meanwhile, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

Ramayana is the second-highest-grossing Hindi movie in India as of Friday, and the fourth-highest-grossing Indian movie ever. body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Hanuman Ansh star Shobhinaw Satyaa compares his journey to Shah Rukh Khan. more Shobhinaw Satyaa compares his journey to SRK In conversation with Variety India, Shobhinaw opened up that he joined Hanuman Ansh as an assistant director to Vishal Chaturvedi. However, since the director was unable to find the right star for the role of Neem Karoli Baba, he asked Shobhinaw to play the part, as he felt the latter resembled the spiritual leader. Speaking about how he unexpectedly landed the lead role, Shobhinaw compared his journey to that of Shah Rukh Khan , who was initially supposed to play a smaller character in his debut television series Fauji before eventually becoming its lead.

Adding to this, Shobhinaw told Variety India, "Shah Rukh Khan’s story is that he was playing a small character in the Fauji series. The star playing the lead had some other project. He was the director’s son. Shah Rukh Khan was made the hero of Fauji. Changes happen randomly sometimes. The same thing happened to me. I was working as an assistant director in the movie, and the director (Vishal Chaturvedi) told me that I am its hero."

title: Sukesh Chandrashekhar serves legal notice to Netflix over upcoming documentary Love, Scam aur Dhokha; seeks postponement of release
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

The legal notice, issued by Advocate Anant Malik on November 26, follows Netflix's announcement that the documentary will premiere on December 18, 2026. It has been addressed to Netflix Entertainment Services India LLP, Netflix Inc., the India Today Group entity behind India Today Originals, and the documentary's directors and executive producer. The notice gives the recipients 72 hours to respond.

Adding to this, According to the notice, the allegations surrounding the alleged Rs. 200 crore rupees extortion case and incidents inside Tihar Jail are still being examined by courts. Anantam Legal has argued that releasing a documentary presenting one version of these contested events while prosecution witnesses are still being examined could influence public perception and potentially affect the ongoing proceedings.

Meanwhile, The legal team has also raised questions about the people interviewed for the documentary, including whether any prosecution witnesses, investigating officers or serving and former prison officials have participated. It has sought clarification on whether the makers obtained any official documents or recordings from investigating agencies or prison authorities.

Notably, The notice further states that Chandrashekhar was not approached by the documentary's makers and has not participated in the project. It also points out that he has pleaded not guilty in the pending cases and maintains that he is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

As per the latest buzz, Among its demands, Anantam Legal has asked Netflix and the India Today Group to defer the documentary, including its trailers and promotional material, until prosecution evidence in the listed trials is concluded. The team has also sought a complete pre-rollout screening for counsel, disclosure of the people featured in the documentary and preservation of all footage, recordings, scripts and related correspondence.
In further updates, Additionally, the notice seeks the withdrawal of promotional material describing Chandrashekhar as a "conman" or presenting allegations under trial as established facts.

On top of that, Clarifying the legal team's position, he added, "This is not an attempt to silence anyone, and it is not a case against documentaries. It is about timing. A movie can be rolled out a few months later and lose nothing. A trial cannot be run twice."

The legal team has also submitted a representation to the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and the Union Home Ministry, seeking an examination of the documentary before its rollout. Anantam Legal has shared that Chandrashekhar is moving the Delhi High Court to seek postponement of the rollout and a direction for the court to view the documentary before it reaches audiences.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

title: Sudesh Berry reacts to daughter-in-law, ex-Roadie Shambhavi Sharma's claim that he didn't support her acting career
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sudesh Berry spoke about daughter-in-law Shambhavi Sharma's recent comments. more 'If you don't have it in your fate, nobody can help you' In an interview with SCREEN, Sudesh shared he has always encouraged newcomers in the industry, irrespective of whether they are related to him. He also described Shambhavi as his daughter but shared he could not help her achieve something that was not destined for her.

Adding to this, He shared, "I've always encouraged every newcomer I've come across in the industry, whether we're related or not. Shambhavi is not just my daughter-in-law, but my daughter. They're all my sons and daughters. But I can't help them achieve something that's not in their destiny. I've never chased stardom myself, so how can I help either her or my son get it? I've always had faith in a higher power. If stardom is in your fate, nobody can stop you from getting it. Similarly, if you don't have it in your fate, nobody can help you achieve it either. Shambhavi, as her name suggests, is a form of goddess herself. So, why does she need me to help her out with her career?"

Meanwhile, The star also shared he did not wish to comment further on Shambhavi's statements, adding that he was content with his life. He shared, "Whatever she's saying reflects her state of being. My state of being is very different. I'm just grateful to be at my happiest and healthiest at 60+. That's what was in my destiny. Whether you're Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Dilip Kumar or Amitabh Bachchan, it was in your destiny that you'd become a superstar. That's what they've maintained too."

Notably, In conversation with Siddharth Kannan, Shambhavi recalled meeting Suraj shortly after participating in MTV Roadies 5.0 in 2007. She was 18 at the time. The two were also supposed to star together in a movie titled The Little Godfather, backed by Ekta Kapoor's Balaji Motion Pictures and Suniel Shetty's Popcorn Motion Pictures. However, the project was shelved, and the two continued their relationship.

As per the latest buzz, When Suraj proposed marriage, he suggested that they move to Australia, where several of Shambhavi's family members lived. She shared she received little support from his family and had expected her marriage into a Bollywood family to help her stay connected to the entertainment industry.

In further updates, She shared, "I told my parents that I'm getting married into a Bollywood family. I thought it'd be amazing, but I had no help. His father probably helped him the first few months with paying the rent, but that's it. I thought being married into a Bollywood family, I'd still be able to keep in touch with my media work. Maybe my father-in-law would promote me. Maybe I'll get his contacts, but nothing of that kind happened. I kept going very far from my dreams."

On top of that, Shambhavi opened up that she eventually took up odd jobs to support the household before moving into corporate roles, even rising to the rank of a CEO. She also shared that she and Suraj are now separated and that divorce proceedings are underway.

title: Supreme Court declines urgent hearing on petition challenging Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The development came after the petitioner's counsel sought an early hearing, alleging that the movie presented a distorted version of the Indian epic. The lawyer argued that certain aspects of the story had been misrepresented and expressed concern about the impact such portrayals could have on younger audiences.
Adding to this, "I am just saying one thing because many facts are distorted. It is a new generation which is coming," the counsel submitted before the bench.

Meanwhile, Responding to the submission, CJI Surya Kant questioned the need to involve the court over differences in interpretation of the epic. He suggested that those who disagreed with the movie's portrayal could present their own interpretation through another cinematic work.

Notably, "They have made a movie as they understand. You make your movie as you want. Don't waste time of the Court. If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view," the Chief Justice remarked.

As per the latest buzz, Despite the court's observations, the petitioner's counsel continued to request an early listing. However, the CJI reiterated that the issue of urgency was central to the request, particularly since the movie was already running in theatres.

In further updates, "We are only concerned with the urgency because you are mentioning the matter. Urgency is not there in the matter because the movie is already rolled out. It is there in theatres. People are watching. People can have their own view. There's no doubt about it. There may be somebody who will praise, somebody will say something critical. This is perfectly respectable. You make any movie, any documentary," he shared.
On top of that, Ramayana , an adaptation of the Indian epic, was rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.
The Supreme Court's observation focused on the request for an urgent hearing, with the bench noting that audiences were free to form their own opinions about the movie.

Adding to this, One of the boldest moves this veteran director has ever made with his movie's heroine is having her enter a men's washroom to speak to her husband's boss and resolve a legal dispute. And that's probably the most daring that things get in his otherwise squeakyclean cinematic universe. Maine Pyaar Kiya and Hum Aapke Hain Koun! carved a niche for Sooraj Barjatya, creating a genre that has become synonymous with him. But in an age of speed dating and hookups, where does his latest family drama, Yeh Prem Mol Liya, stand? Let's find out.

Meanwhile, The story revolves around, no prizes for guessing, Prem (Ayushmann Khurrana), a struggling musician who first lays eyes on Purva (Sharvari) at a railway station, where she is busy helping some elderly people. It doesn't take long for him to fall in love, and he wastes no time in proposing marriage. However, Purva, the sole breadwinner of an all-women household, has one condition: she won't leave her family to move into Prem's home, as convention dictates. Prem agrees and, along with his grandfather (Anupam Kher), convinces his entire family to move into Purva's house instead. The friction that follows forms the crux of the movie.

Notably, Sooraj, who has also written the movie, has an interesting premise on his hands. If you took the risk of watching Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri last year, the Kartik Aaryan-Ananya Panday starrer, you would know that it explored a similar idea. However, as I had pointed out in my review back then, that movie's biggest flaw was that it introduced the boy-moving-into-the-girl's-house angle only in the second half. Sooraj, on the other hand, lays the groundwork for it right from the first half, and until the interval, the proceedings are an absolute breeze. We are introduced to a bunch of quirky characters, one after another, and time flies. But then comes the melodrama.

As per the latest buzz, The second half of Yeh Prem Mol Liya is largely consumed by drama, and it can test your patience at times. The pace slackens after the interval, with one problem after another cropping up for the newlywed couple. The climax, however, redeems the movie to some extent. The messaging, which touches upon women's empowerment, male privilege and archaic notions of how a woman is expected to behave after marriage (phew, the number is quite a lot), is rather heavy handed. Not that we are complaining about the ideas themselves, but a little subtlety wouldn't have hurt. And at 2 hours and 53 minutes, the movie could certainly have done with some trimming by editor Shweta Venkat Mathew.
In further updates, What works in the movie's favour is its soothing music and background score, composed by Himesh Reshammiya and George Joseph, respectively.

On top of that, Coming to the performances, Sharvari looks completely at ease, slipping into the Sooraj Barjatya universe effortlessly. She looks beautiful and, more importantly, never overdoes the innocence that the role demands. Ayushmann, who had the added pressure of being inevitably compared to the OG Prem, Salman Khan, puts up a good show. The two share a pleasant chemistry, making their pairing work. Among the ensemble, my top picks are Supriya Pathak Kapur and Geeta Agrawal Sharma, both of whom are wonderful in their respective roles. Anupam Kher, a Barjatya veteran, is as dependable as ever. Swanand Kirkire as Prem's dad is okay.

Overall, Yeh Prem Mol Liya may not be Sooraj Barjatya's finest work, but it has enough warmth and old school charm to make for a reasonably entertaining watch. The first half is better even if the movie loses some steam once the melodrama takes over. Still, if you enjoy Barjatya's familiar world of big families and uncomplicat3ed romance, there is enough here to keep you occupied. Just don't expect him to suddenly embrace the world of dating apps and casual hookups. Some things, it seems, are never going to change in the Barjatya universe. And perhaps that's precisely the point.

title: Manoj Bajpayee recalls pestering Naseeruddin Shah while drunk during first meeting, says actor would have hit him
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Manoj Bajpayee spoke about meeting Naseeruddin Shah for the first time. more Manoj Bajpayee on meeting Naseeruddin Shah while drunk Manoj shared that Naseeruddin was initially considered for the role of Man Singh in Bandit Queen, but he turned it down. The role eventually went to Manoj. The two actors met for the first time at the movie's wrap-up party in Delhi.

Adding to this, Recalling the incident in a conversation with The HFF News, Manoj shared, “I was quite a rebellion back then, and at the time of Bandit Queen’s wrap up party, Naseer sahab (sir) was in Delhi around that time. So, Shekhar Kapur (filmmaker and director of Bandit Queen) invited him over, and shared, ‘Come, also meet the boy who played your role.’ So, he came, and by the time he arrived, we had already consumed free alcohol. I was also drunk. Naseer sahab would do English plays back then, and I got stuck on that topic: ‘Why do you do English theatre?’ I would follow him everywhere and ask the same question.”

Meanwhile, Manoj shared his repeated questions irritated Naseeruddin, who almost hit him. However, the two left the past behind and later worked together in the movie Drohkaal. He shared, “Naseeruddin Shah is quite an angry person, and all my friends were trying to save me from him. Otherwise, he would have really hit me that day. He was also avoiding me and saying, ‘I don’t want to talk to this person’. So, that incident was so ingrained his memory that he never forgot my face. The moment he saw me on the set of Drohkaal, he shared, ‘Oh, barkhurdaar, aaiye aaiye’ (Come young man, come!) And, from there, we started getting to know each other.”

Notably, Directed by Shekhar Kapur, Bandit Queen was based on the life of Phoolan Devi. Seema Biswas played the titular role, while Manoj Bajpayee Nirmal Pandey, Rajesh Vivek, Saurabh Shukla and others played key roles.
As per the latest buzz, The movie won several honours, including the National Movie Award for Best Feature Movie in Hindi.

title: SCOOP: Salman Khan plans MASSIVE star-studded Maatrubhumi premiere in Mumbai; his first as a leading man in 7 years
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A source told Bollywood Hungama , “Salman Khan is toying with the idea of organizing a premiere of Maatrubhumi , most probably on December 2 in Mumbai. He’s happy with the way the movie has shaped up. He has already shown the war drama to a few of his close friends and now wants to showcase it to prominent members of the Bollywood fraternity as well. Hence, he is planning a premiere.”

Adding to this, The source continued, “If the plan materializes, it’ll be a star-studded affair for sure. The whole industry loves and adores Salman Khan and is expected to turn up in full force to watch his movie. Hence, expect the Maatrubhumi premiere to be one of the biggest Bollywood gatherings of the year, if the plan goes ahead.”

Meanwhile, Interestingly, the premiere would also mark a significant development for Salman Khan. An industry insider commented, “This would be the first time in the post-pandemic era that Salman Khan would organize a premiere for a movie featuring him in the lead role. The last time he did so was for his 2019 releases, Bharat and Dabangg 3 . Both premieres witnessed a massive industry turnout and were grand red-carpet extravaganzas.”

Notably, Salman Khan did not host premieres for his subsequent releases as a leading man, such as Kisi Ka Bhai Kisi Ki Jaan (2023), Tiger 3 (2023) and Sikandar (2025). He did, however, organize a premiere for his home production, Farrey (2023). It did not feature him as an star and it marked the acting debut of his niece, Alizeh Agnihotri. He also held the premiere of Antim: The Final Truth (2021), in which he played a supporting role, while Aayush Sharma was the leading man.

title: Sukesh Chandrashekhar serves legal notice to Netflix over documentary Love, Scam aur Dhokha; says it presents one-sided narrative
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Alleged conman Sukesh Chandrashekhar has sent a legal notice to Netflix over a documentary on him. (PTI Photo) (PTI) more Sukesh Chandrashekhar sends legal notice over documentary Anantam Legal, the lawyers for Sukesh, have shared they have asked that the rollout of the documentary be deferred until prosecution evidence has been recorded in the criminal trials the movie focuses on. The notice, issued by Advocate Anant Malik, has given the movie’s makers and Netflix 72 hours to respond. The movie is currently slated for rollout on 18 December.

Adding to this, The notice, a copy of which is with Hindustan Times, says that the allegations made in the movie are part of a court trial. The alleged Rs. 200 crore rupees extortion and the alleged events inside Tihar Jail are the subject of a case before the Special Court (MCOCA), Rouse Avenue Courts. The evidence is currently being recorded in the case, and the next date is 30 November. The notice also states that Sukesh was not approached by the documentary’s makers for his version of the events. Sukesh’s lawyers call the documentary a public trial, saying that he has not been convicted in any of the cases, except one, which is also under appeal.

Meanwhile, Through his lawyers, Sukesh has now demanded not just a deferment of the rollout, but also a pre-screening of the documentary for him, written confirmation that the movie and its trailers will not be rolled out until prosecution evidence in the listed trials is concluded, and withdrawal of publicity material that describes him as a ‘conman’.
Notably, HT has learnt that the makers and Netflix are yet to respond to the notice.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Netflix India (@netflix_in)

In further updates, On Thursday, Netflix revealed the movie, describing it as a story that delves into the extraordinary story of a man accused of orchestrating an elaborate web of deception. The documentary comes from the makers of Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case and The Indrani Mukerjea Story: Buried Truth. According to a press note from Netflix, the movie utilises two years of research to delve into and trace Sukesh’s origin story and explore how he managed to operate on such a scale, even from inside Tihar jail. Directed by Moumita Sen and Niyantha Shekar & executive produced by Chandni Ahlawat Dabas, Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story premieres on Netflix on December 18.

On top of that, Sukesh Chandrashekhar is the alleged mastermind behind a ₹ 200 crore rupees extortion case. It is alleged that while lodged in Delhi's Rohini Jail, Sukesh impersonated senior government officials and allegedly extorted around ₹ 200 crore rupees from Aditi Singh, wife of former Ranbaxy promoter Shivinder Mohan Singh, during 2020-21. He allegedly promised to secure her husband's rollout from jail in exchange for money. The Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) investigated the alleged extortion and filed a chargesheet under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA). Sukesh was eventually sentenced to 8 years in prison in the case. He has appealed against the verdict.

title: Imtiaz Ali says playing Lord Ram will help Ranbir Kapoor a lot in life, praises his Ramayana performance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Imtiaz Ali lauded Ranbir Kapoor’s performance in Ramayana. more 'Playing Lord Ram will help him a lot in life' In conversation with PTI, Imtiaz Ali lauded Ranbir's acting abilities and lauded his portrayal of Lord Rama in Ramayana. The filmmaker also spoke about how playing the revered character could have a lasting impact on the star's life.

Adding to this, Imtiaz shared, "There are certain parts where he was very, very good. He is the best, he is such a great star, and he is very, very good. And it was wonderful to see him. I think that playing Lord Ram will help him a lot in life."

Meanwhile, Imtiaz also spoke about Ranbir's ambition to turn director, revealing that the two had discussed filmmaking even before they worked together. He shared, “Even before Ranbir started to act in my films, he and I had discussed (about directing films), he had already told me that his ambition is to direct. And coming out of the Kapoor family and having a mind like that, it’s not a surprise that he has shared that he would be directing. I would be surprised if he didn’t direct. But let’s see, once he starts actively directing, will he know what it is really about and whether he enjoys that or not. I don’t think he will, I hope that he does not stop acting in order to direct. But he was always more interested in direction than acting."

Notably, In an earlier interview with Top Magazine, Ranbir opened up about how playing Lord Rama in Ramayana changed him as a person. He shared, “I understood not that it would be something like a career-defining move for me, but it was definitely life-defining, you know, it changed my life. It got me closer to understanding the Ramayana, to understanding Lord Rama’s journey. I think it made so many positive changes in my life. You know, my bad habits changed, it changed my value system, the way I look at life, the way I look at loss, the way I look at sacrifice, the way I look at Dharma, and I think I really needed that in my life.”

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic, produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. The first instalment has emerged as a major box-office success, earning over ₹ 1,750 crore rupees worldwide. The second instalment is currently slated for a theatrical rollout in 2028.

title: Ananya Panday talks about AI-generated deepfakes and fake endorsements; says, “We have to put our foot down against non-consensual AI use”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In an exclusive conversation with HT City, Ananya spoke about the growing use of AI and the importance of establishing boundaries around it. The 28-year-old star was granted interim protection of her personality rights by the Bombay High Court earlier this month after approaching the court against the unauthorized use of her identity. The concerns included sexually explicit deepfake images, fake endorsements and AI chatbots impersonating her.

Adding to this, Speaking about the growing presence of the technology, Ananya shared, "AI is obviously a reality we are dealing with. It is funny to say the word 'reality' when it is 'artificial', but it is something we all have to accept; it is a part of our lives."

Meanwhile, The star also acknowledged that AI has made certain technical processes on movie sets easier, particularly when it comes to sound editing. Explaining how the technology has helped reduce the time spent on correcting technical issues, she shared, "Things we would have to earlier take retakes for constantly, due to maybe disturbance... with AI, that has sped up. Cleaning it up is quicker. But when it comes to Al replacing people... that's when it becomes scary. I personally don't feel AI can ever take over human emotion."

Notably, However, Ananya believes that the growing use of AI also calls for greater accountability, especially when the technology is used to create misleading or degrading content involving individuals without their permission. Emphasising the need to take a stand against such practices, she added, "I don't know what is going to happen in the long run, but we have to put our foot down, especially when it is non-consensual, and AI is used against a person to degrade them, or show something that is not true."

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, Ananya is set to return as Bella Choudhary in the second season of her show Call Me Bae . Talking about reprising the character and how audiences will see her journey progress, the star shared, “People are going to see a version of my character that is constantly evolving and growing, and that’s how it should be as time passes."
In further updates, On the work front, Ananya was last seen in the romantic drama Chand Mera Dil , co-starring Lakshya. The movie was rolled out in theatres earlier this year.

title: Kareena Kapoor Khan joins Darasing Khurana for UNICEF’s Hindi mental health podcast ‘On My Mind’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Developed by UNICEF in collaboration with international experts, On My Mind aims to address mental health concerns among teenagers and young people. The Hindi adaptation, created in partnership with UNICEF India’s global team, seeks to make these conversations accessible to Hindi-speaking audiences. Kareena’s segments will serve as the opening and closing portions of both episodes, helping bring attention to the subjects discussed.

Adding to this, The podcast will focus on practical ways young people can understand and deal with mental health challenges. It will cover how to navigate difficult phases, recognise signs that a friend or peer may be struggling, and offer support to someone going through an emotional crisis. The episodes will also discuss self-help techniques, situations that require professional assistance, and the role parents, teachers and educators can play in supporting young people. Listeners will also be directed towards affordable mental health resources.

Meanwhile, Star and philanthropist Darasing Khurana, who is also a Commonwealth Global Youth Ambassador, has recorded and presented both episodes. Speaking about his association with the initiative, Darasing shared, "When I was approached for this initiative, my immediate response was yes. As someone who has been actively advocating for mental health, this felt like a natural extension of the work I have been doing and the awareness I want to create among young people. What makes this initiative particularly meaningful is that it goes beyond simply talking about mental health; it gives young people practical information about recognising challenges, supporting one another and knowing where to seek help. With Kareena Kapoor Khan coming on board, I believe these conversations have the potential to reach a much wider audience across the country. And the fact that the episodes are in Hindi makes them all the more relevant, particularly for young people in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, where access to mental health resources can be more limited and conversations around mental health are still surrounded by stigma and taboo. Language should never be a barrier to understanding mental health or seeking support. I hope these episodes encourage more young people to take that first step, whether for themselves or someone around them.”

Notably, The initiative also aligns with Darasing's ongoing efforts to improve access to mental health support. Through his Pause.Breathe.Talk. Foundation, he works towards making counselling services and conversations around mental well-being more accessible and affordable. His role as a Commonwealth Global Youth Ambassador also involves advocating for youth development, well-being and social inclusion on international platforms.

As per the latest buzz, The Hindi edition of On My Mind is expected to premiere on Spotify towards the end of November 2026, with Kareena and Darasing coming together to bring conversations around mental health to a wider Hindi-speaking audience.

title: Grateful to still have my face on a poster: Esha Deol on career so far
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Grateful to still have my face on a poster: Esha Deol on career so far more Esha, who was of late seen in the movie "Pratap" opposite Amit Sadh, shared she feels fortunate to still be part of the industry and have a place in the hearts of audiences.
Adding to this, "It's amazing. It's lovely. I'm just grateful to still get work and be here and have my face on a poster and a place in your heart," she told PTI in an interview.

Meanwhile, The 45-year-old star shared the roles offered to her have naturally evolved over the years, adding that she herself is no longer drawn to the kind of characters she played in her early 20s.

Notably, "Our lives are so open in the public and mine has always been that way. So the roles that people approach you with do change with time. As an artist, what I did in my early 20s, I would not want to do something like that now. It doesn't resonate with me anymore," she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Daughter of late star Dharmendra and star-politician Hema Malini, Esha made her acting debut with the 2002 movie "Koi Mere Dil Se Poochhe" and went on to feature in films such as "Na Tum Jaano Na Hum", "Yuva", "Kaal", "Dhoom" and "No Entry".

In further updates, Asked whether she had found her genre, the star shared that while her initial ambition was simply to enter the industry and find work, she now wants to explore diverse stories and characters where she can make a meaningful contribution.

On top of that, "As an artist, I think tapping into different stories, different characters is the fun part. Instead of getting stuck to just one thing. It gets monotonous. I am not the kind who likes to get monotonous," she shared.

"The industry observes. When you put yourself out there, then there are these Chinese whispers that 'she is still working' or 'she is doing this project'. Then they start considering you. It's all about how you put yourself out there and how they see you," she added.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film scripts history, is highest-grossing Indian film in 27 countries
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor and Yash. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer is no longer the juggernaut it was when it had seven consecutive days of over ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide gross. Its domestic collection has fallen below ₹ 10 crore rupees net a day. But overseas, it has seen a resurgence in its third week, yet again earning over $1 million a day on Thursday, its 22nd day in theatres. This momentum has carried Ramayana’s domestic collection to ₹ 992 crore rupees net ( ₹ 1185 crore rupees gross). It should cross ₹ 1000 crore rupees on Friday, becoming only the second Hindi movie to do so after Dhurandhar The Revenge.

Adding to this, Overseas, Ramayana turned over a new leaf after a subpar start. Thanks to a solid showing in the US and in niche markets such as Thailand, Vietnam, and Nepal, Ramayana has surpassed $64 million overseas in 22 days. As a result, Ramayana has now collected ₹ 1777 crore rupees worldwide. It is the fourth-highest-grossing Indian movie of all time, and should be in the second spot sometime next week, overtaking Baahubali 2 and Dhurandhar 2.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

Notably, The makers of Ramayana revealed on Thursday that the Nitesh Tiwari movie is now ‘#1 Indian movie all-time’ in 27 countries. The list of countries where Ramayana is now the highest-grossing Indian movie includes major markets such as the United States, the United Kingdom, Indonesia, and Thailand, as well as newer markets like Vietnam, Cambodia, and a host of other European countries. The movie has been particularly popular in Southeast Asia, particularly in territories such as Cambodia and Singapore, where the epic is popular. With Sony Pictures giving it a wide rollout, it has also opened new markets for Bollywood, including countries like Slovakia, Ukraine, Latvia, Georgia, Armenia, and the Caribbean.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is the first part of a duology. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, Ramayana is the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Part 2 is scheduled for rollout in 2028.

title: Amish Tripathi defends Sai Pallavi’s warrior Sita in Ramayana, says Valmiki described her as slaying Ravana in ancient version
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In one sequence, she is shown training young girls in swordplay, while another shows her using a dagger to defend herself against asura soldiers.

Adding to this, In an interview with Screen, Amish shared that various versions of the Ramayana exist, including three attributed to Valmiki. Amish shared that in one of those versions, Valmiki also depicted Sita as a warrior who slayed Ravana herself. “Because we are not taught the Ramayana and the Mahabharata through our education system, we are not aware of all the versions. There is a version called the Adbhuta Ramayana, credited to Valmiki. He wrote three versions: the Valmiki Ramayana, the Adbhuta Ramayana, and the Ananda Ramayana. In Adbhuta Ramayana, the elder, more powerful Ravana was killed by Sita. She was a warrior in that version. It's not a new version. It's an ancient version credited to Valmiki.”

Meanwhile, Amish rose to fame with his Meluha series of books, in which he adapted Lord Shiva’s tale into a historical fiction setting. His second novel series was inspired by the Ramayana, with the second book titled Sita: Warrior of Mithila.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

As per the latest buzz, Amish added that understanding of epics grows over time, and discussions about epics like the Ramayana and the Odyssey are complicated because people are usually aware of only one version. “There was a time when it was believed Homer's Odyssey was a pure fantasy. This was a time when the church in Europe was clamping down on any such stories. But then in 19th-century Europe, Troy was discovered. Yes, the core elements of the Trojan War did happen, although there may have been some magic realism added to it,” he added.

title: Imtiaz Ali is happy to see Tamasha get love from viewers, took film's box office failure as lesson for Main Vaapas Aaun
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Imtiaz Ali and Ranbir Kapoor during the shoot of Tamasha. more What Imtiaz shared In conversation with Galatta Plus, when Imtiaz was asked about Tamasha and how he feels seeing all the love and admiration for the movie even after so many years, he shared, “I feel a movie gets exactly what it deserves. I come from that school. I feel Tamasha might have been a bit complicated. In the attempt of making it sophisticated I might have made it a bit inaccessible and it took a bit of time to reveal itself completely. I am happy about the fact that people are giving it love and associating with it, and even referring to it for life choices.”

Adding to this, Imtiaz then added, “I don't even take all the credit myself because I have also learnt from other things. That is a very huge show of love, and I am very happy for it. But for me, I take it as a lesson to try to make my next movie simpler, to access. That was my target for Main Vaapas Aaunga. Let me make a movie that has sophistication yet is accessible to the audience in the very go.”

Meanwhile, Tamasha is a romantic drama that tracks the life story of Ved (Ranbir Kapoor). He falls in love with a woman named Tara (Deepika Padukone) after spending one week with her on the French island of Corsica, and this journey defines and changes his life forever. Years after this trip, when Tara reconnects with Ved, complications arise. Tamasha delves into the rediscovery of Ved from thereon. The movie's music was scored by AR Rahman. The movie opened well at the ticket-window but then saw its collections drop. It eventually collected just ₹ 67 crore rupees net in India, and a little over ₹ 130 crore rupees gross worldwide. It was declared a flop by trade trackers.

Notably, Meanwhile, Imtiaz tasted success with his last directorial Main Vaapas Aaunga . It stars Diljit Dosanjh, Vedang Raina and Sharvari, and rolled out in theatres on June 12. After moderate numbers on its intital days of rollout, the movie picked up on word-of-mouth and went on to become a hit. title: Ramayana box office collection day 22: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash film stays steady, manages to cross ₹990 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer Ramayana has also made it to two technical shortlists for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards, competing in the Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design categories. more Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. Friday saw a dip, and the movie collected only ₹ 48.05 crore rupees. The movie picked up on Saturday with a haul of ₹ 69.80 crore rupees. The movie then collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday and ₹ 94 crore rupees net on Tuesday, both the highest in Indian cinema history.

Adding to this, In its third week, the movie saw a dip in collections, and to combat this, the movie’s makers have now slashed ticket prices across India. Following the announcement, most halls across India reduced the ticket prices for their Ramayana shows to as low as ₹ 99"> ₹ 99 . This has certainly helped in maintaining the momentum for the movie. The latest update from Sacnilk states that Ramayana collected ₹ 9.65 crore rupees on Thursday, which is a slight growth in comparison to its previous day when the earnings were at ₹ 9.50 crore rupees. This brings the total ticket-window earnings to ₹ 992.10 crore rupees .

Meanwhile, The movie is now in touching distance of the 1000 crore rupees mark, which it should be expected to cross by tomorrow. Despite the dip, the movie has collected over ₹ 1700 crore rupees gross worldwide.

Notably, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra ’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Priyanka Chopra pays tribute to martyrs of 26/11 terror attack in Mumbai, remembers the heroes who gave everything
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Priyanka Chopra penned a note on 18th anniversary of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. (AP) more Priyanka's statement The star took to her Instagram Stories and wrote, "Remembering the lives lost and the heroes who gave everything on 26/11. #MumbaiTerrorAttacks.”

Adding to this, Earlier, star Bhumi Pednekar paid tribute to the Mumbai Police, security forces and first responders who lost their lives while protecting the city. Bhumi attended a tribute ceremony organised by the Maharashtra Police Boys Sanghatana at the Gateway of India in Mumbai. The event marked the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 attacks and also honoured civilians who lost their lives in the Pahalgam terror attack. She attended the ceremony alongside Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

Meanwhile, On November 26, 2008, 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea route in Mumbai and opened fire, killing 166 people, including 18 security personnel, and injuring several others during a 60-hour siege in the city. The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, the Oberoi Trident, the Taj Mahal Hotel, Leopold Cafe, Cama Hospital and the Nariman House Jewish community centre, now renamed Nariman Light House, were some of the places targeted by the terrorists.

Notably, The then Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) chief Hemant Karkare, Mumbai’s Additional Police Commissioner Ashok Kamte, Senior Police Inspector Vijay Salaskar and Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Tukaram Omble were among those killed in the attack. NSG commando Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan was also killed while fighting the terrorists.

As per the latest buzz, Priyanka was last seen in The Bluff, which began streaming on Prime Video on February 25. She will next be seen in Varanasi, directed by SS Rajamouli . title: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting reminds Netflix of 2025 advisory on Pakistani content ahead of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo premiere
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

On May 8, 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed OTT platforms, streaming services and digital intermediaries to stop offering Pakistani-origin content in India. The advisory covered films, web series, songs, podcasts and other digital content, citing national security and public order concerns.

Adding to this, The latest development has brought attention to Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, which is scheduled for a global Netflix premiere on December 4, 2026. The series features Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and other Pakistani actors. However, it is not expected to be available to viewers in India in accordance with the existing advisory.

Meanwhile, The row has also drawn reactions from industry organisations. The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) have as per reports written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding that the series be blocked in India. They have also called for permanent legislation restricting Pakistani entertainment content.
Notably, Netflix has not publicly revealed any change to the series' rollout plans in India. The Ministry's latest communication reiterates the position conveyed under the May 2025 advisory.

title: 'You can not blackmail any government': Karnataka CM Shivakumar to protesting ASHA workers
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Shivakumar shared the protesters should make a similar demand before the Central government and not just the state government because they are recruited by the Centre. (ANI) more He also assured that his government would find a way out, and appealed to them to return to work.

Adding to this, In conversation with reporters in Mysuru, Shivakumar shared the protesters should make a similar demand before the Central government and not just the state government because they are recruited by the Centre.

Meanwhile, "They (ASHA workers) seem to think they can succeed in blackmailing the government. You can't blackmail any government, whether it is mine or any other; such things cannot be done," the chief minister shared.
Notably, "I am once again making a humble appeal to the ASHA workers. Please go back, return to your duties. We will call you and hold discussions with you," he shared.

In further updates, "Whom should I give a written assurance to? If we start doing things this way, it will become a practice across the state. The government also has its limitations and legal constraints. With whom should I enter into an agreement?" he asked.
On top of that, Shivakumar wondered why the ASHA workers were seeking a written assurance from the state government when the central government appointed them.

"Why are they not seeking a written assurance from the central government? Why are they not placing their demands before the Centre? I cannot give written assurances in every such matter. This is not an agreement," Shivakumar shared.
