title: Sharvari Wagh calls marriage the ‘end goal’ of love, opens up about her bridal debut in Yeh Prem Mol Liya
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sharvari Wagh and Ayushmann Khurrana's movie Yeh Prem Mol Liya will rollout on November 27. more The star is all set to embrace the role of a bride for the first time in Sooraj Barjatya’s soon-to-release movie Yeh Prem Mol Liya , opposite Ayushmann Khurrana. In conversation with India Today, Sharvari opened up about what love and happy endings mean to her. She also revealed how her mother got emotional after seeing her dressed as a bride on screen.

Adding to this, Talking how her idea of love and marriage has evolved over the years, Sharvari shared the values she grew up with continue to influence how she looks at relationships. “I come from a very traditional family where love means marriage. When you fall in love with someone and are committed to that person, I think marriage is your end goal. And I believe in that as a person,” she shared.

Meanwhile, Besides speaking about marriage, Sharvari also talked about acting as a bride for the time and how that role turned into a very emotional moment for her family. Interestingly, Sharvaris older sister was getting married at the time the movie was being shot. So when Sharvari was seen on screen as a bride, it brought a wave of emotions for Sharvaris mother.

Notably, “This is the first time I am playing a bride on screen. Interestingly, when we were shooting for this movie, my elder sister was getting married, so we had just had a wedding in the family. When my mother saw me as a bride on screen, she became very emotional. One of her daughters had already left home after getting married, and seeing me like that, she just couldn't stop crying,” Sharvari recalled.

As per the latest buzz, Sharvari also expressed her gratitude to director Sooraj Barjatya for the way he depicted her in the movie. She shared it was a special experience to see herself in such a stunning bridal look on screen.

In further updates, Helmed by Sooraj R Barjatya, Yeh Prem Mol Liya features Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari Wagh in lead roles. The movie also stars Anupam Kher, Supriya Pathak, Seema Pahwa, Saumya Tandon in key roles. The movie is set to rollout on November 27.
On top of that, Dedicated professionals who write about cinema and television in all their vibrancy. Expect views, reviews and news.

title: Legal team of Shah Rukh Khan deny issuing defamation notice to content creator over viral Sadhguru video
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Hirani Associates clarifies that the purported legal notice dated November 23 was neither issued by the superstar nor sent on his instructions.

Adding to this, The clarification comes after several reports claimed that Shah Rukh Khan had initiated legal action against Sharma over an Instagram Reel featuring an interaction between the star, Anant Ambani and spiritual leader Sadhguru at the Global Peace Honours 2026.

Meanwhile, Hirani Associates, which represents the star, dismissed the authenticity of the circulating document and requested media organisations and social media pages to verify the information before attributing the notice to Khan. The law firm also called for the correction or removal of content carrying the purported notice as an official communication from the star.

Notably, Sharing its clarification, Hirani Associates shared, “A purported "legal notice" dated 23 November 2026, shared to have been issued on behalf of Mr. Shah Rukh Khan, is being circulated on social media and in some news reports. As authorised attorneys of Mr. Shah Rukh Khan, we clarify that this notice was not issued by him or on his behalf. Mr. Khan has not instructed any advocate or law firm, including us, to issue it. We request media houses and social media pages to verify before reporting, and to correct or remove content that attributes this notice to Mr. Khan.”

As per the latest buzz, The speculation began after Suvigya Sharma shared an Instagram Reel from the Global Peace Honours 2026. In his commentary accompanying the video, Sharma alleged that Shah Rukh Khan had been asked to “remain silent” during an interaction involving Anant Ambani and Sadhguru.

In further updates, Subsequently, screenshots of a purported legal notice dated November 23 surfaced on social media. The document as per reports referred to Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and listed five demands with a 48-hour deadline for compliance. Sharma also shared a follow-up video reacting to the alleged legal communication.
On top of that, With Hirani Associates now explicitly denying the issuance of the notice, the law firm's statement contradicts the reports linking Shah Rukh Khan to the purported legal action.

Meanwhile, on the professional front, Shah Rukh Khan is preparing for his soon-to-release movie King , directed by Siddharth Anand. The movie marks his first onscreen collaboration with daughter Suhana Khan and also features Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan and Rani Mukerji in the ensemble cast.

title: ‘Journalist status cannot be self-conferred’, Supreme Court says on Delhi anti-CEC protest pleas
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court shared protection for journalists covering Delhi’s anti-CEC protests would depend on their professional credentials, questioning the claims of self-proclaimed journalists. more A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions filed by journalists and media organisations alleging police excesses during the October protests in the Capital. The court shared the protection available to journalists would depend on the nature of their professional credentials and the circumstances in which they sought such protection.

Adding to this, “Examining the standard operating procedure (SOP) read with the stance taken by law enforcement agencies (LEA), it will depend on the character of the person seeking protection,” the bench shared.

Meanwhile, The observations came after the Delhi Police filed an affidavit in response to petitions by journalist unions seeking an inquiry into alleged police excesses. The police shared the evolving digital media landscape had raised questions about whether “reel makers” and “content creators” could be accorded the status of journalists.

Notably, The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, shared journalists working with print publications could be accredited through the Press Council of India, while those employed by television channels could obtain accreditation through the relevant mechanism. Online journalists could also be registered, it shared.

As per the latest buzz, “But we are in the realm of atomised individuals doing journalism. A journalist’s status cannot be self-conferred. Such self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists,” the bench observed.

In further updates, The court was hearing petitions filed by the Free Speech Collective, Delhi Union of Journalists and Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ). The pleas cited separate instances in which media personnel working with established news organisations were allegedly detained or prevented from performing their professional duties during the protests.

On top of that, The bench shared it would examine the broader constitutional questions involved, including the balance between journalists’ right to free movement and the police’s responsibility to maintain law and order.
“If we are called upon to decide the essential issue on balancing of rights, would journalists have a separate species of rights that needs to be seen,” it shared.

title: Samay Raina becomes first YouTube creator globally to cross 1 million channel members
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Samay Raina has touched a major milestone with his YouTube journey. more One million members on YouTube In the latest post from Google India blog, the statement from YouTube team reads, “From host-level banter with Grandmasters to creating the phenomenon that is India’s Got Latent, Samay turned his YouTube channel into the ultimate virtual hangout for millions.”

Adding to this, It added, “Samay's 1-million-channel-member landmark captures a much bigger cultural moment happening across India right now. Audiences aren't just watching from the sidelines anymore; they're choosing to show up for their favorite creators in deeply personal, meaningful ways. In June 2026 alone, more than 1.2 million followers in India bought at least one channel membership on YouTube, driving a 25%+ year-over-year jump in membership revenue for Indian creators.”

Meanwhile, During the finale episode of India's Got Latent season 2, Samay shared, "I never thought this would happen, two years ago when the row first happened, and everything went down. Notably, The row surrounding Samay's India's Got Latent erupted in February 2025 after YouTuber Ranveer Allahbadia made an objectionable remark about parents and incest during an episode. His comment sparked widespread outrage on social media, with several people criticising the panel for crossing the limits of humour in the name of comedy. As per the latest buzz, The backlash intensified after the clip went widely shared, prompting Ranveer to issue a public apology. Samay also apologised and opened up that he had removed all the episodes of the show from his YouTube channel.

title: Ravi Kishan recalls crying after producer refused to pay him ₹1.8 lakh, threatened to remove his role
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ravi Kishan recalls crying after producer refused to pay his remuneration. (Photo: Mustaq Khan/HT) more Producer owed Ravi ₹ 1.8 lakh, paid him only ₹ 8,000 Speaking on Koffee With Karan, where he appeared alongside Akshay Kumar, Ravi recalled working on the 1994 movie Udhaar Ki Zindagi, which also starred Kajol. He shared the producer had promised to pay him ₹ 1,80,000 for his role but gave him only ₹ 8,000 initially, asking him to collect the remaining amount after dubbing. At the time, Ravi's family had mortgaged a piece of agricultural land in their village, and he needed the money to repay the debt and get it rolled out.

Adding to this, He shared, "I had done a movie called Udhaar Ki Zindagi, Kajol starred in that movie. The producer was paying me ₹ 1,80,000 to star in that movie. He only gave me 8K in the beginning and told me that he will give the rest after dubbing. At that time, I had some land in my village which was mortgage and I had to pay off the debt."
Meanwhile, Ravi added that when he approached the producer after completing the dubbing, the latter refused to pay him the remaining amount and even threatened to cut his role from the movie.

Notably, He shared, “So I went for the dubbing. After I finished, I asked him for the money because I had promised my father that I would send money to him for the land, but the producer asked me, ‘What money?’ He told me, ‘If I pay you, I will chop your role out of the movie.’ I told him not to pay me but keep my role in the movie. I had a motorbike, I wore the helmet and cried while driving on my way to bandstand. I didn't take the money."

As per the latest buzz, Akshay, who appeared on the show with Ravi, also recalled facing a similar situation early in his career. However, he chose to confront the producer. Akshay shared that a producer owed him ₹ 68,000, so he went to the producer's house and took a tape recorder. He later sold it for ₹ 32,000 to recover part of his pending payment.

In further updates, Ravi's journey in the movie industry has seen several ups and downs. After struggling to find consistent work in Hindi cinema, he accepted an offer from Bhojpuri producer Mohan Prasad to star in Saiyaan Hamar. The movie went on to become a cult hit and helped revive Bhojpuri cinema. He appeared alongside Salman Khan in Tere Naam (2003) and went on to feature in films such as Welcome to Sajjanpur, Mukkabaaz, Batla House, Singham Again and Laapataa Ladies. His performance in Kiran Rao's Laapataa Ladies (2024) also collected him considerable appreciation.

On top of that, His recent movie credits include Daaku Maharaaj (2025), Son of Sardaar 2 (2025), Maa Behen (2026), Dhamaal 4 (2026) and Mirzapur: The Movie (2026). He has also been seen in the Netflix series Maamla Legal Hai.

Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today. At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through movie reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, star interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing. Now, as Assistant Editor at Hindustan Times Entertainment, Vibha continues to chronicle the world of movies and pop culture. Her work spans breaking entertainment news, exclusive interviews, star features, and stories that capture the conversations shaping Indian cinema.

body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

The movie brings back several familiar characters from the franchise while introducing new faces, including Jaideep Ahlawat and Prakash Raj. Over the years, the Drishyam films have built a following through their suspense-driven storytelling, hidden clues and unexpected developments. The latest instalment continues Vijay Salgaonkar's story as he faces another challenge while trying to protect his family.

Adding to this, Speaking about returning to the character, Ajay Devgn shared, "Vijay Salgaonkar is a character that has stayed with audiences through the years. With Drishyam The Conclusion now coming to Netflix, more people will get to watch the movie. It's always interesting to see how a story reaches different audiences and how they connect with it."

Notably, "Stepping into the world of Drishyam was both exciting and a responsibility. It’s a franchise where audiences remember every detail, question every move and have their own theories. As an star, being part of a story that inspires that kind of investment is incredibly rewarding. What makes Drishyam special is that it challenges the audience as much as it entertains them. I was overjoyed and grateful for all the love and overwhelming response I received for my character and keeps growing each day. With Drishyam: The Conclusion now releasing on Netflix, looking forward to audiences experiencing the same magic and more love," he shared.

title: FWICE writes to PM Narendra Modi, seeks intervention to stop Pakistani Netflix series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo from streaming in India
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:
The federation cites the Centre’s May 2025 advisory on Pakistani-origin content and reiterates its opposition to professional and commercial collaborations.

Adding to this, In a formal communication to the Prime Minister, the federation, which represents artists, technicians, workers and other professionals associated with the Indian movie and television industry, has urged the government to take appropriate measures to stop the series from being streamed in the country.

Meanwhile, FWICE has cited the advisory issued by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on May 8, 2025, which directed OTT platforms, media streaming services and intermediaries operating in India to discontinue content originating from Pakistan. The advisory covered web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content, with national security considerations cited as the reason.

Notably, Reiterating its position on professional associations with Pakistani entertainment industry members, FWICE shared it has issued directives to its affiliated associations and members, asking them to refrain from employing or collaborating with Pakistani actors, singers, musicians, performers, technicians and other professionals across films, television programmes, web series and music videos.

As per the latest buzz, The federation has also called upon its members to avoid participating in, promoting or associating with concerts, cultural programmes, entertainment events and other activities organised by Pakistani individuals or organisations. Its directives further extend to professional, technical and creative assistance, including digital and online collaborations.

In further updates, In its latest communication, FWICE expressed concern over the proposed Indian distribution of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo through an international streaming platform, arguing that the rollout raises questions about the implementation of the government's earlier advisory.

On top of that, The federation also expressed solidarity with the All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA), which as per reports wrote to the Prime Minister on November 24, 2026, seeking a ban on the series' rollout in India.

FWICE has appealed to the Prime Minister and the concerned government ministries to examine the matter and take appropriate action in accordance with applicable laws and government policies. It has also urged OTT platforms, broadcasters, production houses, event organisers, artists and other industry stakeholders to adhere to the government advisory and its non-cooperation directives.

title: Netflix announces documentary on conman Sukesh Chandrashekhar, to premiere on December 18
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Produced by India Today Originals, the team behind Netflix documentaries such as Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case and The Indrani Mukerjea Story: Buried Truth, the project will examine Chandrashekhar's journey from his teenage years in Bengaluru to becoming a prominent figure in several high-profile criminal investigations.

Adding to this, Directed by Moumita Sen and Niyantha Shekar, with Karan Rana as co-director, the documentary draws on more than two years of research. Chandni Ahlawat Dabas serves as the executive producer, while Munish Pandey and Shams Tahir Khan are associated with the project as crime consultants.

Meanwhile, The documentary will look into allegations of an elaborate fraud and extortion network as per reports involving around Rs. 200 crores. It will examine how Chandrashekhar allegedly used fake identities and impersonated senior government officials to gain the trust of his targets. The movie will also explore his reported connections with politicians and Bollywood personalities, including Jacqueline Fernandez, whose name has surfaced in investigations linked to the case.

Notably, Another aspect the documentary will investigate is how Chandrashekhar allegedly continued operating his network while lodged in Delhi's Tihar Jail. It will also examine possible systemic loopholes and the methods he as per reports used to convince people to trust him.

As per the latest buzz, Rather than focusing only on the financial allegations, the project aims to explore the psychology behind the alleged deception and how the operation continued over an extended period.
In further updates, The cases connected to Chandrashekhar remain subject to legal proceedings, and the allegations are yet to be established in court.

title: Mumbai Police issues LOCs against CJP's Saurav Das, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka over Dadar protest last month
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The LoC against CJP spokesperson Saurav Das came to light earlier on Thursday after the Centre informed the Delhi High Court about it. (ANI) more According to Mumbai Police officials, the circulars were issued over an FIR registered against Dipke, Das, Ranka, as well as other CJP members and their supporters on October 3 for allegedly gathering illegally and sloganeering in Dadar.

Adding to this, The police had denied permission to the CJP’s representative Ajinkya Shinde for organising the protest on Gandhi Jayanti at Shivaji Park, saying they were not empowered to grant permission for any gathering at Shivaji Park.
Meanwhile, An LoC is an alert sent to Indian immigration checkpoints at international airports, seaports, and land borders to track or stop the person named from entering or leaving the country.

Notably, The LoC against CJP spokesperson Saurav Das came to light earlier on Thursday after the Centre informed the Delhi High Court about it, stating that it had been done at the request of the Maharashtra Police. Das had moved the HC on Monday (November 23), alleging that he was stopped from travelling to London to deliver a lecture at Oxford University. The CJP had condemned the LoC against Das, saying the outfit spokesperson had not been informed about this when he was stopped at the airport, PTI reported. There was no immediate reaction from the CJP on the LoCs against Dipke and Ranka.

As per the latest buzz, The Shivaji Park police had registered a case against Abhijeet Dipke, Pranav Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, Saurabh Das, Afreen Nawaz, Saumya Korde, Ankit Bharadwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingle over the protest at Shivaji Park last month. The FIR also mentioned 400 CJP supporters, HT reported earlier .

In further updates, “We have registered a case against the organisers of CJP protests on October 2 at Shivaji Park. The case has been registered under sections 189 (unlawful assembly) and 223 (disobedience to a public servant’s lawful order) of the Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and section 37 (power to prohibit certain acts for prevention of disorder) and 135 (disobeying or breaking official orders issued by the police) of the Maharashtra Police Act,” a police personnel from the Shivaji Park Police Station had shared.

On top of that, The cops had denied permission for CJP's October 2 protest citing a judgment of the Bombay High Court in PIL 116/2009 dated January 4, 2013, and a subsequent order of the Maharashtra government dated January 20, 2016. The HC order had restricted the use of Shivaji Park for purposes other than sports. Police had also shared that the organisers had not submitted the required BMC permission for using the ground.
In a separate development this morning, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, submitted before Justice Amit Mahajan that an LoC had been opened against him.

title: SS Rajamouli's Varanasi release may be pushed to August 2027 due to VFX work? Here’s what we know!
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

According to a report by Telugu360, S.S. Rajamouli is holding off on locking in a rollout date until he reviews the final VFX output. Given the movie's massive scale and heavy reliance on CGI, the director wants to ensure the visual effects meet his exact standards before committing. As a result, the project may shift to a late July or August 2027 rollout, with August currently looking like the frontrunner.
Adding to this, However, there has been no official announcement confirming a postponement, and April 7, 2027, remains the revealed rollout date.

Meanwhile, The speculation comes days after the movie's team shared an update on its production progress. On November 15, responding to a fan on X, the official Varanasi handle verified that filming had been completed. It also opened up that post-production, computer-generated imagery (CG) work and re-recording were underway, while dubbing was yet to begin.

title: ‘Self-proclaimed journalists may not get same protection as accredited ones’: SC on anti-CEC protest pleas
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court was hearing pleas filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists. (ANI/ Representational) more The top court was hearing pleas filed by the Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists, who had submitted that their reporters were forcibly removed from protest sites and prevented from recording events, with some also being subjected to physical force, news agency PTI reported.

Adding to this, These petitions were filed by journalist organisations and associations over complaints of police excesses and misconduct by police personnel during the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the Capital last month.
Meanwhile, The top court, in context of the pleas, noted that the status as a journalist “is not self-conferred,” adding that reporters are accredited according to their medium.

Notably, “Status [as a journalist] is not self-conferred. If you're a journalist from a newspaper/print media, you're under [Press Council] accredited journalist...if you are a TV channel of that newspaper you are accredited accordingly...you can also be an online journalist and you can also have registration. These things we have to...we are in the realm of atomized individuals claiming to be journalists. Self proclaimed journalists may not have same protection as accredited journalists,” Justice Joymala Bagchi noted, according to Live Law.

As per the latest buzz, The bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also relegated to a high-powered committee the pleas over the alleged detention of seven journalists, and the alleged assault and obstruction of reporters who were covering protests in Delhi on October 10 and October 11, PTI reported. The committee is headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy.

In further updates, This comes a week after the Delhi Police, in an affidavit filed in response to petitions by journalist organisations and associations, shared there was a need to scertain if “reel makers” and “content creators” can be considered journalists, HT reported earlier .

On top of that, “In the present era of evolving digital media, several individuals, whether creative or otherwise, make reels, upload them and commercially exploit the content created by them. While there can be no objection to such activities, the question as to whether such reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters is yet to be determined,” the affidavit, filed by Joint Commissioner of Police Surender Kumar, shared.

The Supreme Court, while hearing the pleas, shared it would first have to “define” who a journalist is. ""Please appreciate - first we have to define a journalist. Is it a journalist in the category of a profession where someone is registered under the Press Council? Or is employed with a registered newspaper/TV channel? Or a person who seeks to be a (spokesperson) to the citizens, like in social media who are making reels," Live Law cited Justice Bagchi as saying.

title: BREAKING: King expected to be 3 hours and 17 minutes long; could become Shah Rukh Khan’s FIRST film in 20 YEARS to cross the 3-hour mark since Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna

Interestingly, there was a time when Shah Rukh Khan regularly featured in films that ran for more than three hours. Between 2000 and 2006, several of his most memorable films, including Mohabbatein (2000), Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001), Devdas (2002), Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), Veer-Zaara (2004) and Swades (2004), had lengthy runtimes. Mohabbatein , at 3 hours and 35 minutes, ranks among the longest films of his illustrious career.

Adding to this, However, with changing times, filmmakers increasingly began to believe that audiences preferred shorter and crisper films. Interestingly, even Shah Rukh Khan’s Jab Tak Hai Jaan (2012) and Happy New Year (2014) fell just short of the three-hour mark. His more recent blockbusters, Pathaan (2023) and Jawan (2023), had runtimes of 2 hours and 26 minutes and 2 hours and 49 minutes, respectively.

Meanwhile, But life seems to have come full circle. The phenomenal ticket-window success of lengthy films like Animal, Pushpa 2 and Dhurandhar has challenged the perception that modern-day audiences have shorter attention spans. In that sense, it makes perfect sense for a big-ticket entertainer like King to have a runtime of over three hours if the narrative demands it. A longer runtime also gives the makers ample scope to do justice to the movie’s ensemble cast, action sequences and emotional quotient.

title: Ravi Kishan recalls father thrashing him for wearing saree for Ramleela, says he wanted to ‘kill him’ for pursuing acting
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

He opposed the idea so strongly that when Ravi once wore a saree to perform in a Ramleela, his father thrashed him, believing that his son had brought shame to the family.

Meanwhile, Sukesh Chandrashekhar is the alleged mastermind behind a ₹ 200 crore rupees extortion case. It is alleged that while lodged in Delhi's Rohini Jail, Sukesh impersonated senior government officials and allegedly extorted around ₹ 200 crore rupees from Aditi Singh, wife of former Ranbaxy promoter Shivinder Mohan Singh, during 2020-21. He allegedly promised to secure her husband's rollout from jail in exchange for money. The Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) investigated the alleged extortion and filed a chargesheet under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA). Sukesh was eventually sentenced to 8 years in prison in the case.

Notably, The case gained prominence after investigations revealed Sukesh’s connections to Bollywood actors Jacqueline Fernandez and Nora Fatehi . Both actors have maintained they knew nothing about Sukesh’s alleged criminal activities. In her statement recorded before the court, Nora shared she merely attended an event organised by Leena Maria Paul, Sukesh's associate, where she met him for the first time in December 2020.

As per the latest buzz, Jacqueline also claimed that she was unaware of Sukesh’s alleged illegal businesses. However, in June, a Delhi Court directed that charges be framed against her in the case, noting that there was sufficient prima facie material indicating that Jacqueline received luxurious gifts from Sukesh Chandrasekhar despite being aware of his criminal activities. While framing charges, the court shared: “She was in connivance with Sukesh Chandrasekhar to conceal the use of proceeds of crime.” Since the case had been exposed, Jacqueline has maintained that she was a victim, not a willing participant in the scam.

title: Ramayana refuses to slow down even in its FOURTH week; Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Gunmaaster G9 face a tricky show-sharing battle
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A trade source told Bollywood Hungama , “The distributors of both films want maximum shows for their respective films. However, the runtime of Yeh Prem Mol Liya is 2 hours and 53 minutes while that of Gunmaaster G9 is 2 hours and 22 minutes. Hence, dividing the shows equally is not possible at several cinemas. Most single-screen theatres can play five shows at the most and hence, one movie will have to make do with fewer shows than the other.”

Adding to this, The trade source continued, “But that’s not all. The distributors of Ramayana have also asked for a show in single-screen cinemas since their movie continues to do well. The advance booking for the fourth weekend is also encouraging. Hence, not just single-screen theatres but even two-screen cinemas are finding it challenging to adhere to the directives of the distributors of Ramayana, Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Gunmaaster G9 .”

Meanwhile, As of 9:00 am on November 26, advance bookings for Friday were yet to commence at several single-screen cinemas in Mumbai like Regal, Maratha Mandir, New Excelsior, Roxy, Citylight, INOX Dadar, MovieTime Dahisar, Star City, Chitra, Plaza, Maxus Kandivali, Mukta A2 Santacruz, Kasturba, Gold Cinemas in Borivali, Thane, Dadar and Santacruz, PVR Le Reve, MovieTime Suburbia, Bharatmata, Premiere Dongri, Anand Thane, Vaishali Badlapur, Venus Ulhasnagar, Woodland Virar, Gopi Dombivali and Ajanta Cinex Borivali.

Notably, Meanwhile, several two-screen cinemas, including SunCity, MovieTime Malad, MovieMax V Cinema, Cinepolis Shaan, K Movie Star, Iconix Thane, Rasaaz, Topiwala and Miraj Anupam in Goregaon, Rajhans Ghatkopar and PVR Milap, were also yet to commence bookings.

As per the latest buzz, Interestingly, Bharat Cineplex in Kurla is among the exceptions in the two-screen category. The cinema has decided to allot five shows to Yeh Prem Mol Liya , four shows to Gunmaaster G9 and one show to the Marathi movie, Gana Dhav Re .

In further updates, On the single-screen front, two cinemas have commenced bookings. Nishat in Grant Road will exclusively screen Gunmaaster G9 with four shows a day. MovieMax Andheri, meanwhile, has opted for a more balanced approach, allotting two shows each to Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Gunmaaster G9 and retaining one show of Ramayana . Many in the trade believe that the MovieMax Andheri model could be the most practical solution to the ongoing show-sharing tussle. It, however, remains to be seen whether the distributors of all three films agree to such an arrangement and allow other cinemas to follow suit.

title: Salman Khan, 60, learnt action choreography in 10 minutes, reveals Maatrubhumi co-star Jayson Thaam; recalls ‘tough’ shoot during red alert in Leh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Jayson Thaam is a part of Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace. more In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, Jayson Shah talked about his journey to becoming an star, how Maatrubhumi was the toughest shoot of his life and heaped praise on Salman Khan. The star revealed how Salman learnt the action choreography in just 10 mins while other actors, younger than him, took over an hour.

Adding to this, Jayson always knew that he wanted to be part of the entertainment industry. He eventually took the plunge, starting out as a background dancer around 2010-11. After participating in a reality show, he moved to Mumbai with the ambition of becoming a choreographer. He began assisting and choreographing for reality shows before landing a role in Channel V's Dil Dosti Dance, which became a turning point in his career and made him realise that acting was where he wanted to be.

Meanwhile, Talking about Maatrubhumi, Jayson called it one of the toughest shoots of his life. He shared, "It was physically and mentally tough because everything was against us. The weather: there was a red alert going on during our shoot when we were shooting in Leh. And three more films were shooting with us in different locations. They had all been cancelled. They shared that they won't be shooting for the next 3-4 days because they don't want to endanger anyone."

Notably, However, Jayson opened up that the Maatrubhumi team didn't back out and shot for all four days. He added, "There were landslides, there were rocks falling from the mountains, heavy rain. We did the toughest action sequences during those days. So just imagine, we were so prepared for this shoot.

As per the latest buzz, Jayson shared he knew the opportunity to be part of Maatrubhumi was not one to be missed. Aware of the challenges of shooting at high altitudes, he doubled down on his physical training, running for up to an hour and a half to build his stamina and endurance. He also worked on his diet and researched soldiers through interviews and documentaries to understand their lifestyles, routines and body language to prepare for his character.

In further updates, Jayson was all praise for Salman Khan's fitness and agility, saying, "Don't get deceived by his age. He is very young. I think he's fitter than most of us." Recalling the action rehearsals, he shared it took the team at least an hour or two to learn the choreography, while Salman took barely 10 minutes. "The action choreographers were telling him, 'Sir, yeh yeh karna, yeh yeh karna.' He shared, 'Show it to me again.' Then he did it himself and shared, 'Okay, let's do it then.' I was shocked. He was doing everything, the tumble, the rolls, everything possible," Jayson recalled. He added that Salman had surprised everyone on set and off it, saying, "Physically, he is 21 years old, honestly. Age has nothing to do with that man."

On top of that, He also lauded Salman's cheeky sense of humour, adding, "A lot of people don't get his sense of humour. They don't give enough credit for his sense of humour. He has a very cheeky humour. Mischievous side to him because sometimes he'll say something to you with a straight face and then you take a moment to realise that he's pulling your leg, man. So I think that's a very entertaining part of him and that's what I love about him. I love that man."

While the songs Madirapan and Teri Sexy Beauty in Maatrubhumi invited criticism, Jayson defended them, saying, "I mean, soldiers can't have fun or what? When you see the movie, you'll know why the song has been there, why the songs are placed in the movie. It's very easy to judge that this song should not have been there in a war movie. It's not a war movie, man. It's the life of the soldiers and their lives. It's not based on one event. So, it's unfair to say that. It's based on the whole a soldier going to the border and also his life in his house with his family. And soldiers have fun. People will understand the meaning of the song, and why it has been kept, once they watch the movie."

title: With Dhurandhar, Prahaar, and Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata, Bollywood finally learnt how to depict 26/11 on screen
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dalvinder Saini (centre) played Ajmal Kasab in Dhurandhar. more Hindi cinema’s attempts to recreate the night of 26/11 almost always fell short until the last 12 months. Three films depicted the horrors of the night in three completely different manners and in three different genres. And surprisingly, all of them hit the mark. 2026 was the year when Bollywood finally learnt how to depict its city’s greatest tragedy in an impactful, yet sensitive manner.

Adding to this, Bollywood’s attempts to recreate 26/11 on screen began rather prematurely. Ram Gopal Varma accompanied then Maharashtra chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and his son, star Riteish Deshmukh, to the Taj Mahal Hotel just days after the attacks. The filmmaker and Deshmukh were both criticised for it. RGV eventually made his movie, The Attacks of 26/11, in 2013. But the Nana Patekar-starrer was widely criticised for being too self-indulgent.

Meanwhile, In contrast, when Anthony Maras made Hotel Mumbai five years later, the audiences were swept away. The Dev Patel, Anupam Kher, and Jason Isaacs-starrer was hailed for its impactful depiction of the horrors of that night. It took Hollywood to set the ball rolling, and Indian streaming followed. Nikkhil Advani’s Mumbai Diaries streamed on Prime Video in 2021, and told the story of the night through the eyes of medical professionals treating the injured. The Telugu movie, Major, recreated the incident with a cross-sectional look at the heroics of Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan. It managed to capture the essence of the attacks much better than whatever Hindi cinema had tried.

Notably, Aditya Dhar’s Dhurandhar, rolled out just days after the 26/11 anniversary, recreated the attacks with chilling accuracy and unprecedented impact. The movie, the story of an Indian spy embedded in Pakistan, recreated the deaths and the mayhem, showing how the handlers and terror financiers in Pakistan celebrated through all of it. The jarring contrast between the bloodshed and laughter was enhanced by Ranveer Singh ’s flawless performance and director Dhar’s choice to include real audio from the night.

As per the latest buzz, Akshaye Khanna and Arjun Rampal both ‘broke down and cried uncontrollably’ after filming the scene, castmate R Madhavan recalled. Arjun called the scene ‘my revenge for whatever I saw that night’. The star recalled that night. “In the morning, when I drove back home, I had to stop at least three times because I thought I was going to be sick. When Aditya Dhar narrated to me the 26/11 scene, I knew I was going to have my revenge, and that's what I did with Dhurandhar.”

In further updates, Many viewers shared they felt repulsed or enraged in theatres; such was the scene’s impact. 26/11 survivor Rajita Bagga wrote on social media, “To see the scene recreated from the other side- the handlers celebrating at every bomb going off & every person killed - if that doesn’t fill us with rage and renewed commitment to national security, what else will? 17 years have passed, but the memory of what happened and what could have happened to us just shook me to the core. Gut-wrenching and painful.”

On top of that, But if Dhurandhar brought the brutality and ferocity of the night into focus, Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata chose to focus on the compassion caregivers showed. Like Mumbai Diaries, the movie focused on medical professionals’ experiences of the night. The Kangana Ranaut -starrer chose to tell the story through the eyes of the nurses at Cama Hospital, who turned the hospital into a cantonment and protected patients against the attackers, saving 20 pregnant women in the maternity ward.

Rajkummar Rao-starrer Prahaar chose to focus on the aftermath of the incident, particularly on public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam’s crusade to convict the lone surviving attacker, Ajmal Kasab. Talking of the movie’s take, Nikam himself shared that he wanted no ‘glorification’ of anyone, including himself. "My first condition was there would be no glorification of any character, including me. And all the real names would be used,” he shared. This was a departure from how Hindi cinema usually deals with films about real events, in which names are changed, and characters are invented. Prahaar may have collected mixed reviews, but audiences and critics alike lauded its tonal shift and attempt to show real as real.

title: Dulquer Salmaan compares himself to Salman Khan, says he isn't enough to make a film bankable

I don't think I am enough to make a movie bankable. I think it needs more, including substance and some amount of 'truth or honesty.'"

title: Vinod Kapri's 'Pyre' sets UAE, UK release date
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vinod Kapri's 'Pyre' sets UAE, UK rollout date Deepa Bharath is handling the movie's UAE distribution, while Amandeep Dhillon's ReelIn UK is distributing it in the United Kingdom, according to a press rollout.

Adding to this, Featuring debut actors Padam Singh Kapri and Heera Devi, the movie is set against the backdrop of the Kumaon Himalayas. It explores the challenges of migration from Himalayan villages and the enduring value of love and companionship in the later stages of life.

In further updates, "'Pyre' is a heartfelt and compelling cinematic experience that transcends geographical boundaries. We are proud to bring this beautiful movie to audiences in the UAE and UK and hope its universal themes of love, relationships and human connection resonate with viewers," they shared in a note.

Kapri also received the Best Director award at movie festivals in Serbia and Boston.

title: Jaideep Ahlawat joins Raymond Chairman’s Collection as ‘Friend of the Brand’; brings retro Bollywood style back in focus
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The star’s association with the label will revisit the fashion influences of Indian cinema from the 60s, 70s and 80s through a contemporary take on bespoke dressing.

Adding to this, The association was unveiled at an invitation-only event held on November 25 at the Raymond Chairman’s Collection flagship store in Bandra, Mumbai. The showcase explored the changing fashion aesthetics of Indian cinema across the three decades and their influence on popular culture and menswear. Through the collection, Raymond presented a range of looks that combine retro influences with contemporary tailoring, craftsmanship and detailing.

Meanwhile, Speaking about his association with the brand, Jaideep Ahlawat shared, “I’m a lifelong student of cinema. Movies have taught me a thing or two about attitude, character and, of course, style. Talking about style, retro is cool again, and nostalgia is part of pop culture. So, when Raymond Chairman’s Collection gave me the chance to recreate the stylish decades of the ’60s, ’70s and ’80s for today’s well-traveled man, it was a privilege. Styled thoughtfully and meticulously crafted, the three looks showcase the pinnacle of bespoke luxury. The attention to detail made it even more personal. I’m delighted to be the face of the campaign and the new brand friend of Raymond Chairman’s Collection.”

Notably, Satyaki Ghosh, Whole-time Director and CEO of Raymond Lifestyle Limited, also spoke about the collaboration and the brand’s approach to the collection. He shared, “Raymond’s 101-year legacy has been shaped by its ability to evolve with generations while remaining rooted in craftsmanship. Raymond Chairman’s Collection, the flagship luxury store is the next step of the legacy for and as connoisseurs of bespoke luxury. Our association with Jaideep, as ‘Friend of the Brand’ with is distinctive screen presence and immense versatility brings an exciting cinematic dimension to this journey. We aim to reinterpret the iconic style influences of Indian cinema through a contemporary lens, celebrating the intersection of culture, fashion and bespoke luxury. It is about translating the nostalgia of the past into a distinctive expression of modern menswear and we are looking forward to see Raymond Chairman’s Collection chronicle styles of Bollywood with Jaideep.”

As per the latest buzz, The event also brought together a select audience for a presentation of the curated looks, their inspirations and the styling choices connecting classic cinematic influences with contemporary luxury menswear. Through the association with Ahlawat, Raymond Chairman’s Collection aims to bring the fashion legacy of Indian cinema into focus while presenting it for a modern audience.

title: Gunmaaster G9 box office prediction: Emraan Hashmi set for his 2nd biggest opening in 14 years, Aditya Datt film poised for ₹8 crore start
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Gunmaaster G9 stars Emraan Hashmi in the lead role. Gunmaaster G9 advance bookings Advance bookings for Gunmaaster G9 opened just two days before the rollout. In 24 hours, the movie had sold tickets worth ₹ 3 crore rupees across all six days. The opening day gross stands at ₹ 80 lakh, with over 32K tickets sold. The Aditya Datt-directed movie is neck and neck with the other Bollywood rollout of the week - Sooraj Barjatya’s Yeh Prem Mol Liya, which has grossed ₹ 84 lakh in advance bookings, but sold fewer tickets at 29K.

Adding to this, Trade insiders are bullish about Gunmaaster G9’s prospects on its opening day, due to good interest in smaller centres and the Hindi heartland, particularly among the young crowd who have adopted Emraan Hashmi as their favourite star over the last couple of years. The movie is poised to earn ₹ 8 crore rupees net on its opening day, according to liberal estimates. Even the more scathing conservative estimates say the movie should earn over ₹ 6 crore rupees on its rollout day.

Meanwhile, Either way, the movie is poised for one of Emraan’s best starts ever. If it does get to ₹ 8 crore rupees, it will be the star’s second-best opening day since 2012, when Raaz 3 opened at over ₹ 10 crore rupees. In the intervening years, only one Emraan Hashmi movie - Awarapan 2 - crossed that. That happened just three months ago when the much-awaited sequel opened at ₹ 21 crore rupees and went on to gross ₹ 213 crore rupees worldwide.

Notably, Gunmaaster G9 brings Emraan, director Aditya Datt and composer Himesh Reshammiya together again, nearly two decades after their 2005 movie Aashiq Banaya Aapne. The movie also stars Genelia D'Souza and Aparshakti Khurrana in lead roles. The trailer also makes room for romance with Afsaana Banaaya Aapne, sung and composed by Himesh, featuring Asees Kaur. The song plays as Genelia's character tries to convince Emraan's character not to let their past affect their relationship.
As per the latest buzz, The movie is produced by Deepak Mukut, Hunar Mukut and Sangeeta Ahir. It is scheduled for worldwide rollout in theatres on November 27.

title: Ravi Kishan explains why he calls himself Bihar Ka Brad Pitt on Koffee With Karan, says ‘nobody promotes us’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ravi Kishan of late graced Karan Johar's Koffee With Karan season 9. more Ravi Kishan reveals why he calls himself ‘Bihar ka Brad Pitt’ When Karan asked him about his 'Bihar Ka Brad Pitt' tag, Ravi explained, "One thing I have learnt from life after enduring so many blows is that nobody is going to promote us. title: Akshay Kumar says big people in Bollywood don't cast him due to his 8-hour shift rule, compares working style with Tom Cruise and Christopher Nolan
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Akshay Kumar says he has lost films due to 8-hour work shift demand. more Akshay Kumar on eight-hour work shift costing him films During the episode, when Karan lauded Akshay for giving debutant directors a chance and being considerate towards both producers and directors, Akshay shared, “A lot of big people don’t want to cast me. There are a lot of rumours; they say I work for only eight hours. But they forget that I don’t even go to my vanity van for those eight hours. Our work is to be in front of the camera, and people want to see you beautiful in front of the camera, not tired. So I thought I would work eight hours, sleep for eight hours, spend two hours on my physique and dedicate a few hours to my family.”

Adding to this, Ravi lauded Akshay's speed and energy on movie sets, saying that the star also helps producers save money by wrapping up films quickly. He added that Akshay usually completes a movie in around 55 days, which benefits producers and provides employment to the 300-400 people who are part of a movie unit.

Meanwhile, Akshay then added that many people question how he manages to finish a movie in 65 days. He shared, “I of late read an interview with Christopher Nolan, and apparently he doesn’t take more than 90 days to complete a movie. Tom Cruise completed Mission: Impossible in 55 days.”

Notably, In 2025, Deepika Padukone's reported exit from Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Spirit over her eight-hour shift demand sparked a debate about work-life balance for actors. Later, the producers of Kalki 2898 AD also opened up that Deepika would not be part of the movie's sequel. Soon after the announcement, reports about the star demanding an eight-hour work shift and a share in the profits surfaced online.

As per the latest buzz, In October 2025, Deepika defended her eight-hour work demand in an interview with CNBC-TV18. She pointed out that several male superstars in the industry had followed eight-hour shifts for years without facing similar scrutiny. She added that being a woman should not make her request seem pushy. Alia Bhatt, Karan Johar, Neha Dhupia and others came out in support of the star.

In further updates, Akshay will next be seen in Rohit Shetty's Golmaal 5. The fifth instalment of the comedy franchise will also star Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Kunal Kemmu, Sharman Joshi, Shreyas Talpade and Tusshar Kapoor. title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film beats Pushpa 2’s lifetime haul in 3 weeks, crosses ₹1750 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer is no longer the juggernaut it was when it had seven consecutive days of over ₹ 100 crore rupees in worldwide gross. Its domestic collection has fallen below ₹ 10 crore rupees net per day, and its worldwide gross no longer exceeds ₹ 20 crore rupees per day. Yet, the carried momentum is so strong that Ramayana is still outpacing the biggest Indian blockbusters. In its third week at the ticket window, Ramayana has already netted over ₹ 100 crore rupees in India, becoming the first Indian movie to do so. On Wednesday, it collected ₹ 9.60 crore rupees net, taking its domestic haul to ₹ 982 crore rupees net ( ₹ 1174 crore rupees gross). The movie should touch the ₹ 1000-crore rupees mark by Saturday, making it the fourth Indian movie to do so, after Baahubali 2, Pushpa 2, and Dhurandhar 2.

Adding to this, Overseas, Ramayana turned over a new leaf after a subpar start, and then fell again, only to have a second resurgence in its third weekend. Thanks to a solid showing in the US and in niche markets such as Thailand, Vietnam, and Nepal, Ramayana has surpassed $63 million overseas in 21 days. As a result, Ramayana has now collected ₹ 1755 crore rupees worldwide.

Meanwhile, On Wednesday, Ramayana eclipsed the ₹ 1742-crore rupees haul of Pushpa 2, displacing it in the list of the highest-grossing Indian films. It is now just ₹ 33 crore rupees short of Baahubali 2’s ₹ 1788 crore rupees mark. Given its momentum, it should cross that figure on Friday. After that, the movie only has two huge milestones to look forward to - the ₹ 2000 crore rupees mark and Dangal’s all-time record of ₹ 2070 crore rupees. But to get there, Ramayana would need an additional push, which can only come if the movie secures big releases in China and Japan, as planned.

Notably, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

As per the latest buzz, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. title: Akshay Kumar recalls confronting producer over unpaid dues, taking his tape recorder and selling it for ₹32K
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Akshay Kumar shares wild story of taking producer’s tape recorder after he refused to pay his ₹68,000 dues. more Ravi Kishan recalls giving up his fees for a movie Ravi spoke about his experience working on Udhar Ki Zindagi, which starred Kajol and Jeetendra. The star had a small part in the movie and was expecting a payment of over ₹ 1 lakh. However, after he completed the dubbing, the producer as per reports gave him a difficult choice: he could either receive his full payment or have his scenes retained in the movie.

Adding to this, Ravi shared he was in desperate need of money at the time, as his family's land in their village had been mortgaged. Despite the financial strain, he chose to give up the remaining payment rather than lose the opportunity. For him, staying in the movie was more important as he continued trying to establish himself in the industry.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram Akshay Kumar says he took a producer's tape recorder Akshay related to Ravi's experience and recalled a similar incident from his own struggling days. He shared a producer had failed to pay him around ₹ 68,000, which was a considerable amount for him at the time. After his attempts to recover the money went nowhere, Akshay decided to confront the producer at his home in Mahim.

Notably, Recalling the incident, he shared, “He didn't pay me, and the movie had flopped too. But I needed my money. Around ₹ 68,000 was still pending, which was a lot for me at the time. I went to his house in Mahim in Mumbai and rang the doorbell. He opened the door. He was a short man, so I looked down at him, and he looked up at me. He understood that I had come to collect my money. I then looked inside the house, saw a tape recorder in the hall, unplugged it and took it with me. I was very angry because he hadn't paid me. He didn't stop me either. I sold it at Heera Panna for ₹ 32,000. Even today, he has never returned my money,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Akshay shared he was so frustrated by the producer's refusal to pay him that he decided to take the tape recorder home. He later sold it at Heera Panna for ₹ 32,000, recovering only part of what he was owed. The star added that the producer never paid him the balance.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The show will bring together singles from different backgrounds and personalities as they interact and explore the possibility of finding a romantic connection. Created by Adhiksha Gupta and Mohammed Nagaman Lateef, the format will focus on conversations, relationships and the dynamics that emerge when people meet for the first time.

Adding to this, Akanksha Chamola, who is among the participants, spoke about stepping outside her comfort zone through the show. It's going to be challenging at times for sure but also very surprising,” she shared.

Notably, Commenting on the launch, Sanjay Dwivedi, Group CEO and Group CFO of Balaji Telefilms, shared the company is looking to explore new formats as digital viewing habits evolve. “At Balaji Telefilms, our focus has always been on identifying evolving audience preferences and translating them into engaging entertainment experiences. As the digital entertainment landscape continues to grow, we see immense opportunities to experiment with fresh concepts, distinctive formats and stories that resonate with audiences across platforms. With It's A Meal, we are bringing an interesting take on relationships and matchmaking, packaged in an entertaining format,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Mohammed Nagaman Lateef, Head of Talent at Balaji Telefilms' talent division Hoonur, also spoke about the idea behind the show. “The idea behind It's A Meal was to of course to make the journey of finding a connection entertaining and engaging. body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The meeting follows protests by the Indian Youth Congress in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram over alleged restrictions on accounts critical of the BJP. (Reuters) more According to people aware of the matter, Meta was represented by Aman Jain and Natasha Jog from its public policy team, who explained the US-based social media firm’s three broad objectives — its content moderation policy; its neutrality towards all political parties; and the firm’s concerns about its employees being targeted across the country.

Adding to this, To be sure, the company in its latest transparency report disclosed a massive spike in content takedowns in India -- from 70,000 in 2025 to over 5 million in just the first six months of 2026 on government takedown orders.

Meanwhile, The meeting comes after the Congress’s youth wing issued a seven-day ultimatum to Meta on November 20? over alleged restrictions on accounts and posts critical of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). In a post on X, the IYC urged Meta to operate as a neutral platform and restore the restricted accounts and posts and warned of legal action and street protests, and shared it would “storm your offices across the country” unless the accounts were restored.
Notably, However, the Meta did not commit to any of the conditions at the Tuesday meeting, people cited above shared.

As per the latest buzz, In a statement to HT, a Meta spokesperson shared posting, uploading, sharing or transmitting content in the categories prohibited under the Information Technology (IT) Rules is barred on its platforms. “These prohibitions apply equally to synthetically generated information – content created or substantially modified using artificial intelligence, machine learning or other computational tools, including deepfakes and AI-generated text, images, audio and video,” the spokesperson shared.

In further updates, The company shared it makes “reasonable and appropriate efforts” to keep such content off its platforms. It uses automated tools to detect and review potentially violating content under its Community Standards, and “automatically restrict[s] access to certain types of content in India based on legal requirements under IT Rules”. It also relies on reports from users, and reviews and acts on “valid legal orders” from authorised government agencies and courts in India. Content that is reported or detected is checked against Meta’s Community Standards and/or Indian law.

On top of that, When Meta finds that content violates Indian law, it may restrict access to individual posts, images or videos in India, the spokesperson shared. It may also temporarily or permanently restrict an account under the IT Rules or when a valid legal order covers it. Users are notified in both cases, the company shared.

The Congress didn’t offer any official statement on the meeting. A senior leader aware of the details added that Supriya Shrinate raised the issue of Meta’s alleged discrimination in dealing with the BJP and the Congress. They highlighted how the Indian Youth Congress chief’s account was temporarily blocked by Meta and questioned how Meta could ensure impartiality and treat the BJP and Congress equally.

title: Madhu Mantena’s Mad Man Pictures issues public notice against Phantom Studios over Rs. 8.10 cr bank guarantee; rights of 17 films including Queen, Singham, Super 30, 83 under legal cloud
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The public notice, dated November 25, 2026, and published in Komal Nahta’s Movie Information, pertains to an order passed by the Bombay High Court on August 13, 2025, in a commercial arbitration petition filed by Mad Man Pictures against Phantom Studios.

Adding to this, According to the notice, the court had recorded an undertaking given by Phantom Studios to furnish a bank guarantee of Rs. 8.10 crores. Until the guarantee was furnished, Phantom had undertaken not to alienate or create third-party rights in certain assets and properties listed in a service agreement dated November 19, 2024.

Meanwhile, Mad Man Pictures has alleged that despite filing a contempt petition in 2026 and repeated extensions granted to Phantom Studios, the last of which expired on October 28, 2026, the bank guarantee has not been furnished. Consequently, Mad Man Pictures maintains that the undertaking continues to remain operational.

Notably, What makes the development particularly significant is the impressive library of films covered by the notice. As per the schedule, Phantom holds a 50% share in the IP ownership of 13 films, including Lootera, Udta Punjab, Shaandaar, Hasee Toh Phasee, Mukkabaaz, NH10, Manmarziyaan, Queen, Masaan, Bhavesh Joshi Superhero, Raman Raghav, Singham and Singham Returns .
As per the latest buzz, Its shared share in the remaining four films stands at 40% in Trapped , 37.50% in 83 , 30.50% in Super 30 and 25% in the Gujarati movie Wrong Side Raju .

In further updates, What also stands out is the involvement of some of Bollywood’s biggest production houses and personalities as co-producers of these films. The list includes Dharma Productions ( Shaandaar, Hasee Toh Phasee ), Balaji Motion Pictures ( Lootera, Udta Punjab ), Reliance Big Entertainment Studio ( 83, Singham, Singham Returns ), Eros International ( NH10, Manmarziyaan, Bhavesh Joshi Superhero, Mukkabaaz ) and Colour Yellow Productions ( Mukkabaaz ). Among the prominent industry personalities named as co-producers in the schedule are Hrithik Roshan ( Super 30 ), Ranveer Singh and Kabir Khan ( 83 ) and Rajkummar Rao ( Trapped ).

On top of that, Through the notice, Mad Man Pictures has cautioned prospective buyers and licensees against acquiring Phantom’s rights in these films, warning that such transactions could invite legal consequences, including contempt of court proceedings.

title: Ravi Kishan was struggling financially and had no work after Tere Naam; reveals how Bhojpuri cinema turned his career around
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ravi Kishan reveals how one Bhojpuri movie rescued his career after work dried up following Tere Naam. more Ravi Kishan on how Bhojpuri cinema changed his career Ravi recalled receiving a call from Bhojpuri producer Mohan Prasad, who offered him a movie. “I was tired of looking for work. One day, I got a call from Mohan Prasad, a well-known Bhojpuri producer. He told me there was a movie he wanted me to do. I asked my mother, 'There's a Bhojpuri movie. Should I do it?' I was hesitant because nobody was really watching films in that industry. It was almost shut down. Sujit Kumar was the last superstar to come out of Bhojpuri cinema. My mother told me to go ahead and do it. She shared that even if nothing else happened, people in our village would at least get to see me,” he shared on the show.

Adding to this, View this post on Instagram The movie was Saiyan Hamaar, which went on to become a cult hit. Ravi shared he was in a difficult place financially and professionally at the time. Even after working with Salman Khan in Tere Naam, he had not found the opportunities he hoped for in Hindi cinema. The Bhojpuri movie, however, gave him a fresh start.

Meanwhile, “I made the movie, and it became a cult hit. It also helped revive an industry. Everything I had learnt while working in Hindi cinema, I put into Bhojpuri films. At that time, Hindi cinema was looking towards the West and trying to make films with a more international flavour. That gave me the space to do something different. While people were making pizza and burgers in Hindi cinema, I decided to serve litti chokha in Bhojpuri films. It worked for me, and my films started doing well. I was working back-to-back and doing three or four shifts a day,” he added.

Notably, Listening to Ravi's journey, Akshay agreed with his approach of continuing to work rather than waiting for the perfect opportunity. He also pointed to Kishan's career as an example of what persistence can achieve. “This is exactly what I want to say. Keep making films. Do two or three films. Keep working. Look at the way he has done it,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Ravi has continued to move between mainstream Hindi cinema and projects in other languages. In recent years, he has been seen in Laapataa Ladies and the Netflix series Maamla Legal Hai . His more recent movie credits include Maa Behen, Dhamaal 4, Peddi, Aryabhatt Ka Zero and Mirzapur: The Movie, which was rolled out in September 2026.

In further updates, He is also part of several soon-to-release projects. These include Naagzilla, Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 and Mera Yaar Bajrangi. He is set to headline a movie by Bengali filmmaker duo Nandita Roy and Shiboprosad Mukherjee, which will explore the growing influence of Korean culture in India. The project is expected to go on floors in early 2027.

She is among the few Indian journalists in India with a dedicated focus on Korean entertainment, including K-pop and K-dramas, and has interviewed some of the industry's biggest stars while closely tracking the rise of global pop culture. title: Varun Dhawan, DJ Chetas, Ayan Agnihotri back franchises at Prospect Padel League auction; women's players attract higher bids
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The eight franchises are backed by PadelPark India, Varun Dhawan and Mokksh Sani, Ranjit Bindra and Zeeshan Siddique, Naagarjun Sethuppathy, Kartik Reddy, DJ Chetas and Suraj Samat, Being Human Clothing and Ayan Agnihotri, and Rana Digvijay Sinh Kathiwada and Abhishek Mohan Gupta.

Adding to this, One of the key highlights of the auction was the bidding for women players, who collectively attracted 2.38 million virtual points, compared to 2.29 million virtual points for the men's category, according to the organisers. Steisha Buddhala received the highest individual bid of 5.7 million virtual points from Vice Indian. Amarjot Kaur Bundhel followed with 5.1 million virtual points for RB All Stars, while Ethan Bardo attracted 5 million virtual points from BH Racqueteers Padel Club.

Meanwhile, The 16 marquee players collectively attracted bids worth 40.67 million virtual points. Among the franchises, Vice Indian recorded the highest combined allocation of 9.7 million virtual points, followed by RB All Stars at 7.5 million and East Coast Warriors at 7.1 million.

Notably, Speaking about the league, co-founder Sahil Shah shared, “Padel is growing fast, and we wanted to build more than a tournament. The Prospect Padel League brings together sport, travel, entertainment and people, creating a destination that extends beyond the game. The auction is an important first step in bringing this vision to life.”

As per the latest buzz, Co-founder Siddhesh Sunil Shinde highlighted the league's focus on creating opportunities for young players. He shared, “Sport has the power to bring young people together. With PPL, we want to build a community where the next generation finds opportunity, ambition and a place to belong. Our approach is centred on recognising talent and giving every player the opportunity to contribute and be valued.”

In further updates, Dheeraj Jain, another co-founder, added, “A great idea is only the beginning. The real magic lies in making it happen. With our hands-on approach, we are building a league that players, teams and followers will remember long after the last match is played. The auction has given us a strong foundation for what lies ahead in Goa.”

On top of that, The first season of the Prospect Padel League is scheduled from December 17 to 21, 2026, at Sunday Racquet & Social Club in Goa. Eight franchises will compete for a prize pool of Rs 30 lakhs.

The organisers plan to combine the sporting competition with hospitality and entertainment activities, including private charter travel for players and franchise owners, social gatherings, music and food experiences. The league will follow a Davis Cup-style format alongside its franchise-based competition.

Adding to this, He wrote, “Atif and Honey dancing the night away at a friend’s wedding! And what a lovely sight it was to see them dancing to Abrar-ul-Haq's songs too. Honey walked in looking every inch like an icon that he is. Full of love and warmth and style on point. And then came Atif. Calm, composed and unassuming as ever. He kept his promise and showed up straight from rehearsals for his concert.”

Meanwhile, He added, “I had the pleasure of hosting the evening as the emcee. This was also one of the commitments that meant I couldn't fly down to Karachi for #JBHSSL. Some promises are meant to be kept! And while a complaint is being filed to stop a Pakistani Netflix series from airing, here we are celebrating music, friendship and good times. ❤️ Can happen only in Dubai!”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sadiq Saleem (@sadiqidas)

As per the latest buzz, After the show's trailer rollout, All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, requesting that Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo not be rolled out or streamed on Netflix India. The letter referred to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's advisory issued on May 8, 2025, which asked streaming platforms in India to stop streaming Pakistani content.

On top of that, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo is based on Farhat Ishtiaq’s Urdu romantic novel of the same name. The show stars Ahad Raza Mir, Hania Aamir, Sanam Saeed, Iqra Aziz and Mahira Khan, among others. Created and directed by Momina Duraid, it is set to premiere on Netflix on December 4.

title: Ayushmann Khurrana says he has rejected potential hits that didn't align with his values, calls toxic love ‘problematic’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ayushmann Khurrana says he has never been one to choose a movie purely because it could become a box-office success. more Ayushmann Khurrana on toxic love In conversation with India Today, Ayushmann was asked if Bollywood’s portrayal of romance sometimes bothers him. He shared there is room for different kinds of films and audiences, but unhealthy love can have serious consequences. “Any kind of toxic love is problematic. It's just bad for mental health, I think,” he shared. “I don't know what to say because there is every kind of movie for every kind of audience. That's for sure”.

Adding to this, He shared he wants the films he chooses to make to convey the right message. According to him, a character who behaves toxically should not be presented as an ideal romantic partner. He feels this is an important part of his responsibility as an artist. “But I really believe the kind of films that I have done, the messaging should be correct, and the toxic person should be labelled as a negative guy. I think these are the basics I believe in as an artist. But as I shared, there is a movie for every kind. To each his own, I think. It's not my kind, but there are actors who want to do that. There is a huge audience for that," he shared. “I am somebody who will say no to a movie even if I feel the movie is a hit. I have done that in the past. Films have to resonate with my core”.

Meanwhile, Yeh Prem Mol Liya, which also features Sharvari , is scheduled to rollout in cinemas on November 27, 2026. title: Sharvari says ‘no hard feelings’ over Main Vaapas Aaunga missing Oscar entry, calls Gondhal incredible
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sharvari spoke about Gondhal beating Main Vaapas Aaunga to be India's official entry for Oscars. more 'Gondhal is an incredible movie' Each year, the Movie Federation of India sends one movie to represent the country in the International Feature Movie category at the Oscars. "Any win is a big win for us, it is not about which movie gets selected, it's not a race. Gondhal is an incredible movie, I've watched it myself. It is a Marathi movie and I'm very very proud of it as well. It's a great movie; it has a lot to say to the world. And it's superb that movie has gone ahead," Sharvari told PTI in an interview.
Adding to this, Sharvari recalled the journey Main Vaapas Aaunga had in theatres before emerging as a sleeper hit of 2026, and shared the movie created a "certain trend" in the industry.

Meanwhile, The movie had a slow start in its opening week but positive reviews and strong word of mouth helped it grow at the ticket-window, where it has grossed ₹ 99.39 crore rupees, as per Sacnilk, a trade tracking website.

Notably, "The way it started unfortunately wasn't the best, there were times when people didn't think that it was a movie that was supposed to come in the theatres, and that movie came through. And it had a lot of courage. I think it was Imtiaz sir's vision. I think the audiences really showed, and they gave us so much love. So, it's okay if we didn't go to the Oscars. I think the love of the audience is much bigger than anything else," she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Starring Naseeruddin Shah, Diljit Dosanjh, and Vedang Raina in lead roles, the movie is set against the backdrop of the Partition of India. It follows a young man, Keenu (Raina) who falls in love with Jiya (Sharvari) in the pre-Partition era-a story that unfolds across two timelines, with Shah essaying the older version of Raina's character and Dosanjh playing his grandson.

In further updates, Sharvari is currently looking forward to the rollout of her movie, Yeh Prem Mol Liya, directed by Sooraj Barjatya. She stars opposite Ayushmann Khurrana. She plays Purva, a woman who has a clear point of view and is unwilling to compromise on her responsibilities towards her family.

On top of that, For the 29-year-old star, playing Purva meant balancing the emotional sensitivity that has been a defining feature of the women in Barjatya's films with a contemporary woman who expresses her opinions, which was fun in Yeh Prem Mol Liya.

"I think what has always been consistent in Sooraj sir's films is that the women have a very beautiful soul and heart wherein there is so much respect for everybody in the family. I feel that they are the emotional backbone of all of sir's films and I think that has carried forward even in Purva," she shared.
